children.text: Gopathabrāhmaṇa, Pūrvabhāga, Prathamaḥ prapāṭhakaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Gopatha Brāhmaṇa</s>, Prior Section (<s>Pūrvabhāga</s>), First Lesson (<s>Prathamaḥ prapāṭhakaḥ</s>).

children.text: oṃ brahma ha vā idam agra āsīt svayaṃ tv ekam eva tad aikṣata mahad vai yakṣaṃ tad ekam evāsmi hantāhaṃ mad eva manmātraṃ dvitīyaṃ devaṃ nirmama iti tad abhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat tasya śrāntasya taptasya saṃtaptasya lalāṭe sneho yad ārdryam ājāyata tenānandat tam abravīt mahad vai yakṣaṃ suvedam avidāmaha iti / tad yad abravīt mahad vai yakṣaṃ suvedam avidāmaha iti tasmāt suvedo 'bhavattaṃ vā etaṃ suvedaṃ santaṃ sveda ity ācakṣate / parokṣeṇa parokṣapriyā iva hi devā bhavanti pratyakṣadviṣaḥ || GpBr_1,1.1 ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ. <s>Brahman</s> indeed was this [universe] in the beginning — itself alone, just one. It reflected: 'I am indeed a great being (<s>yakṣa</s>), [and] I am this one alone. Come, let me create from myself a second divine being, equal to my mind.' It exerted itself, it heated itself, it thoroughly heated itself. From the forehead of that exerted, heated, thoroughly heated [Brahman], moisture — a wetness — arose. It rejoiced at that and said: 'A great being (<s>yakṣa</s>) indeed! We have found the well-known (<s>suveda</s>).' Because it said 'A great being! We have found the well-known (<s>suveda</s>),' therefore it became <s>Suveda</s>; but they call that <s>Suveda</s>, which exists, 'sweat' (<s>sveda</s>) — by indirection, for the gods are fond of the indirect and averse to the direct. (GpBr 1,1.1)

children.text: sa bhūyo 'śrāmyad bhūyo 'tapyat bhūya ātmānaṃ samatapat tasya śrāntasya taptasya saṃtaptasya sarvebhyo romagartebhyaḥ pṛthak svedadhārāḥ prāsyandanta / tābhir anandat tad abravīd ābhir vā aham idaṃ sarvaṃ dhārayiṣyāmi yad idaṃ kiṃcābhir vā aham idaṃ sarvaṃ janayiṣyāmi yad idaṃ kiṃcābhir vā aham idaṃ sarvam āpsyāmi yad idaṃ kiṃceti / tad yad abravīd ābhir vā aham idaṃ sarvaṃ dhārayiṣyāmi yad idaṃ kiṃceti tasmāt dhārā abhavaṃs taddhārāṇāṃ dhārātvaṃ yac cāsu dhriyate / tad yad abravīd ābhir vā aham idaṃ sarvaṃ janayiṣyāmi yad idaṃ kiṃceti tasmāj jāyā abhavaṃs tajjāyānāṃ jāyātvaṃ yac cāsu puruṣo jāyate yac ca putraḥ punnāmanarakam anekaśatatāraṃ tasmāt trāti putras tat putrasya putratvam / tad yad abravīd ābhir vā aham idaṃ sarvam āpsyāmi yad idaṃ kiṃceti tasmād āpo 'bhavaṃs tad apām aptvam āpnoti vai sa sarvān kāmān yān kāmayate // GpBr_1,1.2 //
children.translated_text: It exerted itself further, heated itself further, thoroughly heated itself further. From all the pores of that exerted, heated, thoroughly heated [Brahman], separate streams of sweat flowed forth. It rejoiced in them and said: 'By these I shall sustain all this, whatever there is; by these I shall generate all this, whatever there is; by these I shall obtain all this, whatever there is.' Because it said 'By these I shall sustain (<s>dhārayiṣyāmi</s>) all this, whatever there is,' therefore they became streams (<s>dhārā</s>); that is the stream-nature of streams — that which is sustained in them. Because it said 'By these I shall generate all this, whatever there is,' therefore they became wives (<s>jāyā</s>); that is the wife-nature of wives — that a man is born (<s>jāyate</s>) in them, and that a son rescues [one] from the hell named <s>Put</s>, which has innumerable stars; therefore that is the son-nature of a son (<s>putra</s>). Because it said 'By these I shall obtain (<s>āpsyāmi</s>) all this, whatever there is,' therefore they became the waters (<s>āpaḥ</s>); that is the water-nature of waters. He indeed obtains all desires that he desires. (GpBr 1,1.2)

children.text: tā apaḥ sṛṣṭvānvaikṣata tāsu svāṃ chāyām apaśyat tām asyekṣamāṇasya svayaṃ reto 'skandat tad apsu pratyatiṣṭhat tās tatraivābhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat tāḥ śrāntās taptāḥ saṃtaptāḥ sārdham eva retasā dvaidham abhavaṃs tāsām anyā anyatarā atilavaṇā apeyā asvādvyas tā aśāntā retaḥ samudraṃ vṛtvātiṣṭhann athetarāḥ peyāḥ svādvyaḥ śāntās tās tatraivābhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat tābhyaḥ śrāntābhyas taptābhyaḥ saṃtaptābhyo yad reta āsīt tad abhṛjjyata yad abhṛjjyata tasmād bhṛguḥ samabhavat tad bhṛgor bhṛgutvaṃ bhṛgur iva vai sa sarveṣu lokeṣu bhāti ya evaṃ veda // GpBr_1,1.3 //
children.translated_text: Having created those waters, it looked into them and saw its own shadow in them. As it was gazing, its seed spontaneously fell; that seed settled in the waters. It heated those very [waters]; it thoroughly heated them. Those waters, heated, thoroughly heated, together with the seed, split in two. Some of them — the other half — were excessively salty, undrinkable, unpalatable; those, unsettled, encompassing the seed, remained as the ocean. But the others were drinkable, palatable, and calm. It heated those very [waters]; it thoroughly heated them. From those heated, thoroughly heated waters, whatever seed there was — that was roasted (<s>abhṛjjyata</s>). Because it was roasted (<s>abhṛjjyata</s>), from that <s>Bhṛgu</s> came into being. That is the <s>Bhṛgu</s>-nature of <s>Bhṛgu</s>. Like <s>Bhṛgu</s> indeed, he shines in all worlds — whoever knows this. (GpBr 1,1.3)

children.text: sa bhṛguṃ sṛṣṭvāntaradhīyata sa bhṛguḥ sṛṣṭaḥ prāṅ ejatataṃ vāg anvavadad vāyo vāyo iti saṃnyavartata sa dakṣiṇāṃ diśam ejatataṃ vāg anvavadat mātariśvan mātariśvann iti sa nyavartata sa pratīcīṃ diśam ejatataṃ vāg anvavadat pavamānaḥ pavamāna iti sa nyavartata sa udīcīṃ diśam ejatataṃ vāg anvavadad vāta vāteti tam abravīn nanv avidāmaha iti na hīty athārvāṅ enam etāsv evāpsv anviccheti tad yad abravīd athārvāṅ enam etāsv evāpsv anviccheti tad atharvābhavat tad atharvaṇo 'tharvatvam / tasya ha vā etasya bhagavato 'tharvaṇa ṛṣer yatheva brahmaṇī lomāni yathāṅgāni yathā prāṇa evam evāsya sarva ātmā samabhavat tam atharvāṇaṃ brahmābravīt prajāpateḥ prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā pālayasveti / tad yad abravīt prajāpateḥ prajā sṛṣṭvā pālayasveti tasmāt prajāpatir abhavat tat prajāpateḥ prajāpatitvam atharvā vai prajāpatiḥ prajāpatir iva vai sa sarveṣu lokeṣu bhāti ya evaṃ veda // GpBr_1,1.4 //
children.translated_text: Having created <s>Bhṛgu</s>, it disappeared. That <s>Bhṛgu</s>, having been created, moved eastward; Speech followed him saying 'Vāyu! Vāyu!' He turned back. He moved toward the southern direction; Speech followed him saying 'Mātariśvan! Mātariśvan!' He turned back. He moved toward the western direction; Speech followed him saying 'Pavamāna! Pavamāna!' He turned back. He moved toward the northern direction; Speech followed him saying 'Vāta! Vāta!' He [Brahman] said to him: 'Did we not find [him]?' 'No,' [replied Bhṛgu]. 'Then, turning downward, search for him in these very waters.' Because it said 'turning downward (<s>arvāṅ</s>), search for him in these very waters,' that became <s>Atharvan</s>; that is the <s>Atharvan</s>-nature of <s>Atharvan</s>. Of this blessed sage <s>Atharvan</s>, just as are the hairs of <s>Brahman</s>, just as the limbs, just as the breath — so indeed his entire self came into being. <s>Brahman</s> said to that <s>Atharvan</s>: 'Having created the creatures of <s>Prajāpati</s>, protect them!' Because it said 'Having created the creatures of <s>Prajāpati</s>, protect them,' therefore he became <s>Prajāpati</s>; that is the <s>Prajāpati</s>-nature of <s>Prajāpati</s>. <s>Atharvan</s> is indeed <s>Prajāpati</s>. Like <s>Prajāpati</s> indeed, he shines in all worlds — whoever knows this. (GpBr 1,1.4)

children.text: tam atharvāṇam ṛṣim abhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat tasmāc chrāntāt taptāt saṃtaptāt daśatayān atharvaṇa ṛṣīn niramimataikarcān dvyṛcāṃs tṛcāṃś caturṛcān pañcarcān ṣaḍarcān saptarcān aṣṭarcān navarcān daśarcān iti / tān atharvaṇa ṛṣīn abhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat tebhyaḥ śrāntebhyas taptebhyaḥ saṃtaptebhyaḥ daśatayān ātharvaṇān ārṣeyān niramimataikādaśān dvādaśāṃs trayodaśāṃś caturdaśān pañcadaśān ṣoḍaśān saptadaśān aṣṭādaśān navadaśān viṃśān iti / tān atharvaṇa ṛṣīn ātharvaṇāṃś cārṣeyān abhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat tebhyaḥ śrāntebhyas taptebhyaḥ saṃtaptebhyo yān mantrān apaśyat sa ātharvaṇo vedo 'bhavat tam ātharvaṇaṃ vedam abhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat tasmāc chrāntāt taptāt saṃtaptād om iti mana evordhvam akṣaram udakrāmat sa ya icchet sarvair etair atharvabhiś cātharvaṇī kurvīyety etayaiva taṃ mahāvyāhṛtyā kurvīta / sarvair ha vā asyaitair atharvabhiś cātharvaṇaiś ca kṛtaṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda yaś caivaṃ vidvān evam etayā mahāvyāhṛtyā kurute // GpBr_1,1.5 //
children.translated_text: He toiled over, heated, and thoroughly heated that <s>Atharvan</s> seer. From him, toiled over, heated, and thoroughly heated, he produced groups of ten <s>Atharvan</s> seers: those of one verse, two verses, three verses, four verses, five verses, six verses, seven verses, eight verses, nine verses, and ten verses. He toiled over, heated, and thoroughly heated those <s>Atharvan</s> seers. From them, toiled over, heated, and thoroughly heated, he produced groups of ten <s>Ātharvaṇa</s> (descendants of <s>Atharvan</s>) seers' lineages: those of eleven, twelve, thirteen, fourteen, fifteen, sixteen, seventeen, eighteen, nineteen, and twenty [verses]. He toiled over, heated, and thoroughly heated those <s>Atharvan</s> seers and the <s>Ātharvaṇa</s> lineages. From them, toiled over, heated, and thoroughly heated, the <s>mantras</s> which he perceived — that became the <s>Ātharvaṇa Veda</s>. He toiled over, heated, and thoroughly heated that <s>Ātharvaṇa Veda</s>. From it, toiled over, heated, and thoroughly heated, the syllable <s>Om</s> rose upward as the mind itself. He who would wish, 'May I perform with all these <s>Atharvans</s> and <s>Ātharvaṇas</s>' — he should perform with this very <s>Mahāvyāhṛti</s> (great utterance). Indeed, for him who knows thus, it is as if performed with all these <s>Atharvans</s> and <s>Ātharvaṇas</s> — he who knows thus and he who, knowing thus, performs with this <s>Mahāvyāhṛti</s>. // GpBr 1,1.5 //

children.text: sa bhūyo 'śrāmyad bhūyo 'tapyad bhūya ātmānaṃ samatapat sa ātmata eva trīṃl lokān niramimata pṛthivīm antarikṣaṃ divam iti / sa khalu pādābhyām eva pṛthivīṃ niramimatodarād antarikṣam mūrdhno divam / sa tāṃs trīn lokān abhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat tebhyaḥ śrāntebhyas taptebhyaḥ saṃtaptebhyas trīn devān niramimatāgniṃ vāyum ādityam iti / sa khalu pṛthivyā evāgniṃ niramimatāntarikṣād vāyuṃ diva ādityam / sa tāṃs trīn devān abhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat tebhyaḥ śrāntebhyas taptebhyaḥ saṃtaptebhyas trīn vedān niramimata ṛgvedaṃ yajurvedaṃ sāmavedam iti agne ṛgvedaṃ vāyor yajurvedam ādityāt sāmavedam / sa tāṃs trīn vedān abhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat tebhyaḥ śrāntebhyas taptebhyaḥ saṃtaptebhyas tisro mahāvyāhṛtīr niramimata bhūr bhuvaḥ svar iti / bhūr ity ṛgvedāt bhuva iti yajurvedāt svar iti sāmavedāt / sa ya icchet sarvair etais tribhir vedaiḥ kurvīyety etābhir eva taṃ mahāvyāhṛtibhiḥ kurvīta sarvair ha vā asyaitais tribhir vedaiḥ kṛtaṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda yaś caivaṃ vidvān evam etābhir mahāvyāhṛtibhiḥ kurute // GpBr_1,1.6 //
children.translated_text: He toiled further, heated further, and further thoroughly heated himself. From his very self he produced the three worlds: <s>Pṛthivī</s> (earth), <s>Antarikṣa</s> (atmosphere), and <s>Div</s> (heaven). Indeed, from his feet he produced the earth, from his belly the atmosphere, and from his head the heaven. He toiled over, heated, and thoroughly heated those three worlds. From them, toiled over, heated, and thoroughly heated, he produced three gods: <s>Agni</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, and <s>Āditya</s>. Indeed, from the earth he produced <s>Agni</s>, from the atmosphere <s>Vāyu</s>, and from heaven <s>Āditya</s>. He toiled over, heated, and thoroughly heated those three gods. From them, toiled over, heated, and thoroughly heated, he produced the three <s>Vedas</s>: the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, the <s>Yajurveda</s>, and the <s>Sāmaveda</s> — from <s>Agni</s> the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, from <s>Vāyu</s> the <s>Yajurveda</s>, and from <s>Āditya</s> the <s>Sāmaveda</s>. He toiled over, heated, and thoroughly heated those three <s>Vedas</s>. From them, toiled over, heated, and thoroughly heated, he produced the three <s>Mahāvyāhṛtis</s> (great utterances): <s>Bhūḥ</s>, <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, and <s>Svaḥ</s>. <s>Bhūḥ</s> from the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, <s>Bhuvaḥ</s> from the <s>Yajurveda</s>, and <s>Svaḥ</s> from the <s>Sāmaveda</s>. He who would wish, 'May I perform with all these three <s>Vedas</s>' — he should perform with these very <s>Mahāvyāhṛtis</s>. Indeed, for him who knows thus, it is as if performed with all these three <s>Vedas</s> — he who knows thus and he who, knowing thus, performs with these <s>Mahāvyāhṛtis</s>. // GpBr 1,1.6 //

children.text: tā yā amū retaḥ samudraṃ vṛtvātiṣṭhaṃs tāḥ prācyo dakṣiṇācyaḥ pratīcya udīcyaḥ samavadravanta / tad yat samavadravanta tasmāt samudra ucyate / tā bhītā abruvan bhagavantam eva vayaṃ rājānaṃ vṛṇīmaha iti / yac ca vṛtvātiṣṭhaṃs tadvaraṇo 'bhavat taṃ vā etaṃ varaṇaṃ santaṃ varuṇa ity ācakṣate / parokṣeṇa parokṣapriyā iva hi devā bhavanti pratyakṣadviṣaḥ / sa samudrād amucyata sa mucyur abhavat taṃ vā etaṃ mucyuṃ santaṃ mṛtyur ity ācakṣate / parokṣeṇa parokṣapriyā iva hi devā bhavanti pratyakṣadviṣaḥ / taṃ varuṇaṃ mṛtyum abhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat tasya śrāntasya taptasya saṃtaptasya sarvebhyo 'ṅgebhyo raso 'kṣarat so 'ṅgaraso 'bhavat taṃ vā etam aṅgarasaṃ santam aṅgirā ity ācakṣate / parokṣeṇa parokṣapriyā iva hi devā bhavanti pratyakṣadviṣaḥ // GpBr_1,1.7 //
children.translated_text: Those [waters] which, having enveloped the ocean of semen, stood still — they, the eastern, southern, western, and northern [waters], flowed together. Because they flowed together (<s>samavadravanta</s>), therefore it is called <s>samudra</s> (ocean). They, afraid, said: 'Let us indeed choose the Lord himself as our king.' And because they stood enveloping (<s>vṛtvā atiṣṭhan</s>), he became <s>Varaṇa</s> (the chooser). They call this <s>Varaṇa</s> by the name <s>Varuṇa</s> — indirectly, for the gods seem to prefer the indirect and dislike the direct. He was released from the ocean; he became <s>Mucyu</s> (the releaser). They call this <s>Mucyu</s> by the name <s>Mṛtyu</s> (death) — indirectly, for the gods seem to prefer the indirect and dislike the direct. He toiled over, heated, and thoroughly heated that <s>Varuṇa</s>-<s>Mṛtyu</s>. From him, toiled over, heated, and thoroughly heated, the essence (<s>rasa</s>) flowed from all his limbs. He became <s>Aṅgarasa</s> (essence of the limbs). They call this <s>Aṅgarasa</s> by the name <s>Aṅgiras</s> — indirectly, for the gods seem to prefer the indirect and dislike the direct. // GpBr 1,1.7 //

children.text: tam aṅgirasam ṛṣim abhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat tasmāc chrāntāt taptāt saṃtaptād viṃśino 'ṅgirasa ṛṣīn niramimata tān viṃśino 'ṅgirasa ṛṣīn abhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat tebhyaḥ śrāntebhyas taptebhyaḥ saṃtaptebhyo daśatayān āṅgirasān ārṣeyān niramimata ṣoḍaśino 'ṣṭādaśino dvādaśina ekarcāṃs tṛcāṃś caturṛcān pañcarcān ṣaḍarcān dvyṛcān saptarcān iti / tān aṅgirasa ṛṣīn āṅgirasāṃś cārṣeyān abhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat tebhyaḥ śrāntebhyas taptebhyaḥ saṃtaptebhyo yān mantrān apaśyatsa āṅgiraso vedo 'bhavat tam āṅgirasaṃ vedam abhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat tasmāc chrāntāt taptāt saṃtaptāj janad iti dvaitam akṣaraṃ vyabhavat / sa ya icchet sarvair etair aṅgirobhiś cāṅgirasaiś ca kurvīyety etayaiva taṃ mahāvyāhṛtyā kurvīta sarvair ha vā asyaitair aṅgirobhiś cāṅgirasaiś ca kṛtaṃ bhavati ya eva veda yaś caiva vidvān evam etayā mahāvyāhṛtyā kurute // GpBr_1,1.8 //
children.translated_text: He labored and heated [himself] toward the <s>Aṅgiras</s> sage (<s>ṛṣi</s>); he heated and thoroughly heated [himself]. From that [one who was] exhausted, heated, and thoroughly heated, he produced the twenty <s>Aṅgiras</s> sages. He labored and heated toward those twenty <s>Aṅgiras</s> sages; he heated and thoroughly heated [himself]. From those exhausted, heated, and thoroughly heated [sages], he produced the <s>Āṅgirasa</s> descendants in groups of ten — [hymns of] sixteen [verses], eighteen, twelve, single-verse, three-verse, four-verse, five-verse, six-verse, two-verse, and seven-verse. He labored and heated toward those <s>Aṅgiras</s> sages and the <s>Āṅgirasa</s> descendants; he heated and thoroughly heated [himself]. From those exhausted, heated, and thoroughly heated [sages], the <s>mantras</s> that he perceived — that became the <s>Āṅgirasa Veda</s> (Atharvaveda). He labored and heated toward that <s>Āṅgirasa Veda</s>; he heated and thoroughly heated [himself]. From that exhausted, heated, and thoroughly heated [Veda], the two-syllable [utterance] '<s>janad</s>' came forth. Whoever should desire 'May I accomplish [the rite] with all these <s>Aṅgiras</s> [sages] and <s>Āṅgirasas</s>' — he should accomplish it with this very great <s>vyāhṛti</s> (sacred utterance). Indeed, for him it is accomplished with all these <s>Aṅgiras</s> [sages] and <s>Āṅgirasas</s> — he who knows thus, and whoever, knowing thus, performs with this great <s>vyāhṛti</s>. (GpBr 1.1.8)

children.text: sa ūrdhvo 'tiṣṭhat sa imāṃl lokān vyaṣṭabhnāt tasmād aṅgiraso 'dhīyāna ūrdhvas tiṣṭhati tad vrataṃ sa manasā dhyāyed yad vā ahaṃ kiṃcana manasā dhyāsyāmi tathaiva tad bhaviṣyati taddha sma tathaiva bhavati / tad apy etad ṛcoktam / śreṣṭho ha vedas tapaso 'dhijāto brahmajyānāṃ kṣitaye saṃbabhūva ṛjyad bhūtaṃ yad asṛjyatedaṃ niveśanam anṛṇaṃ dūram asyeti / tā vā etā aṅgirasāṃ yāmayo yan menayaḥ karoti menibhir vīryaṃ ya eva veda // GpBr_1,1.9 //
children.translated_text: He stood upright. He propped apart these worlds. Therefore, one who is studying the <s>Aṅgiras</s> [Veda] stands upright — that is the observance (<s>vrata</s>). He meditated with the mind: 'Whatever I shall meditate upon with the mind, that shall become exactly so.' And indeed, it became exactly so. Regarding this, the <s>ṛc</s> (verse) also declares: 'The supreme <s>Veda</s>, born from <s>tapas</s> (austerity), came into being for the protection of the <s>Brahma</s>-knowers. That which was straight — what was created here [became] a resting place, free from debt, extending far.' These indeed are the twinnings (<s>yāmaya</s>) of the <s>Āṅgirasas</s>: whoever creates with the mind-powers (<s>menī</s>), [attains] vigor through the mind-powers — he who knows thus. (GpBr 1.1.9)

children.text: sa diśau 'nvaikṣata prācīṃ dakṣiṇāṃ pratīcīm udīcīṃ dhruvām ūrdhvām iti / tās tatraivābhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat tābhyaḥ śrāntābhyas taptābhyaḥ saṃtaptābhyaḥ pañca vedān niramimata sarpavedaṃ piśācavedam asuravedam itihāsavedaṃ purāṇavedam iti / sa khalu prācyā eva diśaḥ sarpavedaṃ niramimata dakṣiṇasyāḥ piśācavedaṃ pratīcyā asuravedam udīcyā itihāsavedaṃ dhruvāyāś cordhvāyāś ca purāṇavedam / sa tān pañca vedān abhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat tebhyaḥ śrāntebhyas taptebhyaḥ saṃtaptebhyaḥ pañca mahāvyāhṛtīr niramimata vṛdhat karad guhan mahat tad iti / vṛdhad iti sarpavedāt karad iti piśācavedāt guhad ity asuravedāt mahad itītihāsavedāt tad iti purāṇavedāt sa ya icchet sarvair etaiḥ pañcabhir vedaiḥ kurvīyety etābhir eva taṃ mahāvyāhṛtibhiḥ kurvīta sarvair ha vā asyaitaiḥ pañcabhir vedaiḥ kṛtaṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda yaś caivaṃ vidvān evam etābhir mahāvyāhṛtibhiḥ kurute // GpBr_1,1.10 //
children.translated_text: He surveyed the directions — the eastern, southern, western, northern, the fixed (nadir), and the upward (zenith). He labored and heated toward those very [directions]; he heated and thoroughly heated. From those exhausted, heated, and thoroughly heated [directions], he produced five <s>Vedas</s>: the <s>Sarpa-Veda</s> (Serpent-lore), the <s>Piśāca-Veda</s> (Demon-lore), the <s>Asura-Veda</s>, the <s>Itihāsa-Veda</s> (Epic-lore), and the <s>Purāṇa-Veda</s> (Ancient-lore). Indeed, from the eastern direction he produced the <s>Sarpa-Veda</s>; from the southern, the <s>Piśāca-Veda</s>; from the western, the <s>Asura-Veda</s>; from the northern, the <s>Itihāsa-Veda</s>; and from the fixed and upward [directions], the <s>Purāṇa-Veda</s>. He labored and heated toward those five <s>Vedas</s>; he heated and thoroughly heated. From those exhausted, heated, and thoroughly heated [Vedas], he produced five great <s>vyāhṛtis</s> (sacred utterances): '<s>vṛdhat</s>', '<s>karat</s>', '<s>guhat</s>', '<s>mahat</s>', '<s>tat</s>.' '<s>Vṛdhat</s>' from the <s>Sarpa-Veda</s>; '<s>karat</s>' from the <s>Piśāca-Veda</s>; '<s>guhat</s>' from the <s>Asura-Veda</s>; '<s>mahat</s>' from the <s>Itihāsa-Veda</s>; '<s>tat</s>' from the <s>Purāṇa-Veda</s>. Whoever should desire 'May I accomplish [the rite] with all these five <s>Vedas</s>' — he should accomplish it with these very great <s>vyāhṛtis</s>. Indeed, for him it is accomplished with all these five <s>Vedas</s> — he who knows thus, and whoever, knowing thus, performs with these great <s>vyāhṛtis</s>. (GpBr 1.1.10)

children.text: sa āvataś ca parāvataś cānvaikṣata tās tatraivābhyaśrāmyad abhyatapat samatapat tābhyaḥ śrāntābhyas taptābhyaḥ saṃtaptābhyaḥ śam ity ūrdhvam akṣaram udakrāmat / sa ya icchet sarvābhir etābhir āvadbhiś ca parāvadbhiś ca kurvīyety etayaiva taṃ mahāvyāhṛtyā kurvīta sarvābhir ha vā asyaitābhir āvadbhiś ca parāvadbhiś ca kṛtaṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda yaś caivaṃ vidvān evam etayā mahāvyāhṛtyā kurute // GpBr_1,1.11 //
children.translated_text: He surveyed the near and the far [spaces]. He labored and heated toward those very [spaces]; he heated and thoroughly heated. From those exhausted, heated, and thoroughly heated [spaces], the syllable '<s>śam</s>' arose upward. Whoever should desire 'May I accomplish [the rite] with all these near and far [spaces]' — he should accomplish it with this very great <s>vyāhṛti</s>. Indeed, for him it is accomplished with all these near and far [spaces] — he who knows thus, and whoever, knowing thus, performs with this great <s>vyāhṛti</s>. (GpBr 1.1.11)

children.text: sa bhūyo 'śrāmyat bhūyo 'tapyat bhūya ātmānaṃ samatapat sa manasa eva candramasaṃ niramimata nakhebhyo nakṣatrāṇi lomabhya oṣadhivanaspatīn kṣudrebhyaḥ prāṇebhyo 'nyān bahūn devān / sa bhūyo 'śrāmyad bhūyo 'tapyat bhūya ātmānaṃ samatapat sa etaṃ trivṛtaṃ saptatantum ekaviṃśatisaṃsthaṃ yajñam apaśyat / tad apy etad ṛcoktam / agnir yajñaṃ trivṛtaṃ saptatantum iti / athāpy eṣa prākrīḍitaḥ ślokaḥ pratyabhivadati sapta sutyāḥ sapta ca pākayajñā iti // GpBr_1,1.12 //
children.translated_text: He labored again; he performed austerity again; he heated himself again. From his mind he created the moon (<s>Candramās</s>); from his nails, the stars (<s>nakṣatras</s>); from his body-hair, herbs and trees; from his minor vital breaths, many other gods. He labored again; he performed austerity again; he heated himself again. He beheld this sacrifice (<s>yajña</s>), threefold (<s>trivṛt</s>), with seven threads (<s>saptatantu</s>), established in twenty-one [parts]. Regarding this, the <s>Ṛc</s> verse also states: '<s>Agni</s> [beheld] the sacrifice, threefold, with seven threads.' Moreover, this ancient verse (<s>śloka</s>) that was composed in play responds [to this]: 'Seven <s>Soma</s>-pressings and seven <s>pākayajñas</s> (cooked offerings).' // GpBr_1,1.12 //

children.text: tam āharat yenāyajata tasyāgnir hotāsīt vāyur adhvaryuḥ sūrya udgātā candramā brahmā parjanyaḥ sadasya oṣadhivanaspatayaś camasā adhvaryavo viśvedevā hotrakā atharvāṅgiraso goptāras taṃ ha smaitam evaṃ vidvāṃsaḥ pūrve śrotriyā yajñaṃ tataṃ sāvasāya ha smāhety abhivrajanti mā no 'yaṃ gharma udyataḥ pramattānām amṛtāḥ prajāḥ prasākṣīd iti tān vāyetān parirakṣakān sadaḥprasarpakān ity ācakṣate dakṣiṇāsamṛddhāṃs tad u ha smāha prajāpatir yad vai yajñe 'kuśalā ṛtvijo bhavanty acaritino brahmacaryam aparāgyā vā tad vai yajñasya viriṣṭam ity ācakṣate / yajñasya viriṣṭam anuyajamāno viriṣyate yajamānasya viriṣṭam anvṛtvijo viriṣyanta ṛtvijāṃ viriṣṭam anudakṣiṇā viriṣyante dakṣiṇānāṃ viriṣṭam anuyajamānaḥ putrapaśubhir viriṣyate putrapaśūnāṃ viriṣṭam anuyajamānaḥ svarge lokena viriṣyate svargasya lokasya viriṣṭam anu tasyārdhasya yogakṣemo viriṣyate yasminn ardhe yajanta iti brāhmaṇam // GpBr_1,1.13 //
children.translated_text: He brought that [sacrifice] forth; with it he sacrificed. <s>Agni</s> was its <s>hotṛ</s> (invoking priest); <s>Vāyu</s> the <s>adhvaryu</s> (officiating priest); <s>Sūrya</s> the <s>udgātṛ</s> (chanting priest); <s>Candramās</s> (the Moon) the <s>brahmán</s> (supervising priest); <s>Parjanya</s> (the Rain-god) the <s>sadasyá</s> (assessor); herbs and trees the cups (<s>camasa</s>); the <s>Adhvaryus</s> the <s>Viśvedevas</s> (All-gods) as assistant priests (<s>hotraka</s>); and the <s>Atharvāṅgirasas</s> the protectors. The ancient <s>śrotriyas</s> (Veda-knowers) who knew this thus would approach the stretched sacrifice at its conclusion, saying: 'May this heated [offering], raised up, not harm the immortal creatures of those who are inattentive.' Those [priests] they call the guardians, the prowlers at the assembly (<s>sadaḥprasarpaka</s>), well-endowed with sacrificial fees (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>). And <s>Prajāpati</s> declared thus: 'When the priests (<s>ṛtvij</s>) at the sacrifice are unskilled, having not practiced <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate studentship), or are not properly withdrawn—that is called the deficiency (<s>viriṣṭa</s>) of the sacrifice. Following the deficiency of the sacrifice, the sacrificer (<s>yajamāna</s>) suffers deficiency; following the sacrificer's deficiency, the priests suffer deficiency; following the priests' deficiency, the sacrificial fees suffer deficiency; following the fees' deficiency, the sacrificer suffers deficiency in sons and cattle; following the deficiency in sons and cattle, the sacrificer suffers deficiency in the heavenly world; following the deficiency of the heavenly world, the prosperity and welfare of that half [of the world] in which they sacrifice suffers deficiency'—thus [says] the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. // GpBr_1,1.13 //

children.text: taṃ ha smaitam evaṃ vidvāṃsaṃ brahmāṇaṃ yajñaviriṣṭo vā yajñaviriṣṭino vety upādhāveran namas te astu bhagavan yajñasya no viriṣṭaṃ saṃdhehīti tad yatraiva viriṣṭaṃ syāt tatrāgnīn upasamādhāya śāntyudakaṃ kṛtvā pṛthivyai śrotrāyeti trir evāgnīn samprokṣati triḥ paryukṣati triḥ kārayamāṇam ācāmayati ca samprokṣati ca yajñavāstu ca samprokṣaty athāpi vedānāṃ rasena yajñasya viriṣṭaṃ saṃdhīyate tad yathā lavaṇena suvarṇaṃ saṃdadhyāt suvarṇena rajataṃ rajatena lohaṃ lohena sīsaṃ sīsena eṣv evam evāsya yajñasya viriṣṭaṃ saṃdhīyate yajñasya saṃdhitim anu yajamānaḥ saṃdhīyate yajamānasya saṃdhitim anv ṛtvijaḥ saṃdhīyanta ṛtvijāṃ saṃdhitim anu dakṣiṇāḥ saṃdhīyante dakṣiṇānāṃ saṃdhitim anu yajamānaḥ putrapaśubhiḥ saṃdhīyate putrapaśūnāṃ saṃdhitim anu yajamānaḥ svargeṇa lokena saṃdhīyate svargasya lokasya saṃdhitim anu tasyārdhasya yogakṣemaḥ saṃdhīyate yasminn ardhe yajanta iti brāhmaṇam // GpBr_1,1.14 //
children.translated_text: Those who knew this thus would run to the <s>brahmán</s> priest [asking], 'Is there a deficiency of the sacrifice, or [is there one] of those [involved in] the sacrifice-deficiency?' [saying:] 'Homage to you, O blessed one! Restore the deficiency of our sacrifice!' Wherever there was a deficiency, [the priest] would establish the fires there, prepare the waters of appeasement (<s>śāntyudaka</s>), and with [the mantra] 'To the earth, to the hearing,' sprinkle the fires three times, circumsprinkle three times, make the one being purified sip [water] three times and sprinkle, and sprinkle the sacrificial ground. Moreover, by the essence of the <s>Vedas</s>, the deficiency of the sacrifice is restored. Just as one would join gold with salt, silver with gold, copper with silver, lead with copper—in this same way the deficiency of this sacrifice is restored. Following the restoration of the sacrifice, the sacrificer is restored; following the restoration of the sacrificer, the priests are restored; following the restoration of the priests, the sacrificial fees are restored; following the restoration of the fees, the sacrificer is restored in sons and cattle; following the restoration of sons and cattle, the sacrificer is restored with the heavenly world; following the restoration of the heavenly world, the prosperity and welfare of that half [of the world] in which they sacrifice is restored—thus [says] the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. // GpBr_1,1.14 //

children.text: tad u ha smāhātharvā devo vijānan yajñaviriṣṭānandānītpupaśamayeran yajñe prāyaścittiḥ kriyate 'pi ca yad u bahv iva yajñe vilomaḥ kriyate na caivāsya kācanārtir bhavati na ca yajñaviṣkandham upayāty apahanti punar mṛtyum apātyeti punar ājātiṃ kāmacāro 'sya sarveṣu lokeṣu bhāti ya evaṃ veda yaś caivaṃ vidvān brahmā bhavati yasya caiva vidvān brahmā dakṣiṇataḥ sado 'dhyāste yasya caiva vidvān brahmā dakṣiṇata udaṅmukha āsīno yajña ājyāhutīr juhotīti brāhmaṇam // GpBr_1,1.15 //
children.translated_text: And <s>Atharvā</s> the divine, knowing [this], declared: '[Those who know this] would pacify the sorrows of those suffering from sacrifice-deficiency.' When expiation (<s>prāyaścitta</s>) is performed in the sacrifice, even if much that is adverse (<s>viloma</s>) is done in the sacrifice, no harm befalls him, nor does he encounter obstruction of the sacrifice (<s>yajñaviṣkandha</s>). He repels repeated death; he avoids repeated birth. He moves freely in all worlds. He shines forth [thus]—he who knows this, and he who, knowing this, becomes the <s>brahmán</s> priest, and [the sacrificer] whose learned <s>brahmán</s> sits to the south of the assembly, and [the sacrificer] whose learned <s>brahmán</s>, seated facing north to the south, offers ghee oblations (<s>ājyāhuti</s>) in the sacrifice—thus [says] the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. // GpBr_1,1.15 //

children.text: brahma ha vai brahmāṇaṃ puṣkare sasṛje sa khalu brahmā sṛṣṭaś cintām āpede kenāham ekenākṣareṇa sarvāṃś ca kāmān sarvāṃś ca lokān sarvāṃś ca devān sarvāṃś ca vedān sarvāṃś ca yajñān sarvāṃś ca śabdān sarvāś ca vyuṣṭīḥ sarvāṇi ca bhūtāni sthāvarajaṅgamāny anubhaveyam iti sa brahmacaryam acarat sa oṃ ity etad akṣaram apaśyad dvivarṇaṃ caturmātraṃ sarvavyāpi sarvavibhvayātayāmabrahma brāhmīṃ vyāhṛtiṃ brahmadaivataṃ tayā sarvāṃś ca kāmān sarvāṃś ca lokān sarvāṃś ca devān sarvāṃś ca vedān sarvāṃś ca yajñān sarvāṃś ca śabdān sarvāś ca vyuṣṭīḥ sarvāṇi ca bhūtāni sthāvarajaṅgamāny anvabhavat tasya prathamena varṇenāpasnehaś cānvabhavat tasya dvitīyena varṇena tejo jyotīṃṣy anvabhavat // GpBr_1,1.16 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> indeed created <s>Brahmā</s> in the lotus. That <s>Brahmā</s>, having been created, fell into deep thought: 'By what single syllable may I experience all desires, all worlds, all gods, all <s>Veda</s>s, all sacrifices, all sounds, all dawns, and all beings, both stationary and moving?' He practiced <s>brahmacarya</s> (religious studentship). He perceived the syllable Oṃ — having two phonemes, four measures (<s>mātrā</s>s), all-pervading, all-powerful, unfailing — the <s>Brahman</s>, the <s>Brāhmī</s> utterance (<s>vyāhṛti</s>), having <s>Brahman</s> as its deity. By that he experienced all desires, all worlds, all gods, all <s>Veda</s>s, all sacrifices, all sounds, all dawns, and all beings, both stationary and moving. By its first phoneme he experienced the waters and moisture. By its second phoneme he experienced fire and luminous bodies.

children.text: tasya prathamayā svaramātrayā pṛthivīm agnim oṣadhivanaspatīn ṛgvedaṃ bhūr iti vyāhṛtir gāyatraṃ chandas trivṛtaṃ stomaṃ prācīṃ diśaṃ vasantam ṛtuṃ vācam adhyātmaṃ jihvāṃ rasam itīndriyāṇy anvabhavat // GpBr_1,1.17 //
children.translated_text: By its first vowel-measure (<s>svara-mātrā</s>) he experienced the earth, <s>Agni</s> (fire), herbs and trees, the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, the <s>vyāhṛti</s> '<s>Bhūḥ</s>,' the <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter, the <s>Trivṛt</s> <s>stoma</s> (chant-form), the eastern direction, the spring season, and as pertaining to the self (<s>adhyātma</s>) — speech, the tongue, and taste as the sense faculties.

children.text: tasya dvitīyayā svaramātrayāntarikṣaṃ vāyuṃ yajurvedaṃ bhuva iti vyāhṛtis traiṣṭubhaṃ chandaḥ pañcadaśaṃ stomaṃ pratīcīṃ diśaṃ grīṣmam ṛtuṃ prāṇam adhyātmanāsike gandhaghrāṇam itīndriyāṇy anvabhavat // GpBr_1,1.18 //
children.translated_text: By its second vowel-measure he experienced the atmosphere, <s>Vāyu</s> (wind), the <s>Yajurveda</s>, the <s>vyāhṛti</s> '<s>Bhuvaḥ</s>,' the <s>Traiṣṭubha</s> meter, the <s>Pañcadaśa</s> <s>stoma</s>, the western direction, the summer season, and as pertaining to the self — the breath (<s>prāṇa</s>), the nostrils, and smell as the sense faculties.

children.text: tasya tṛtīyayā svaramātrayā divam ādityaṃ sāmavedaṃ svar iti vyāhṛtir jāgataṃ chandaḥ saptadaśaṃ stomam udīcīṃ diśaṃ varṣāṛtuṃ jyotir adhyātmaṃ cakṣuṣī darśanam itīndriyāṇy anvabhavat // GpBr_1,1.19 //
children.translated_text: By its third vowel-measure he experienced heaven, the sun (<s>Āditya</s>), the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, the <s>vyāhṛti</s> '<s>Svaḥ</s>,' the <s>Jāgata</s> meter, the <s>Saptadaśa</s> <s>stoma</s>, the northern direction, the rainy season, and as pertaining to the self — light (<s>jyotis</s>), the two eyes, and sight as the sense faculties.

children.text: tasya vakāramātrayāpaś candramasam atharvavedanakṣatrāṇy o3m iti svam ātmānaṃ janad ity aṅgirasām ānuṣṭubhaṃ chanda ekaviṃśaṃ stomaṃ dakṣiṇāṃ diśaṃ śaradam ṛtuṃ mano'dhyātmaṃ jñānaṃ jñeyam itīndriyāṇy anvabhavat // GpBr_1,1.20 //
children.translated_text: By the measure of the letter 'va' he experienced the waters, the moon, the <s>Atharvaveda</s>, the constellations (<s>nakṣatra</s>s), [the <s>vyāhṛti</s>] 'Oṃ' — his own self — [the <s>vyāhṛti</s>] '<s>janat</s>' of the <s>Āṅgirasa</s>s, the <s>Ānuṣṭubha</s> meter, the <s>Ekaviṃśa</s> <s>stoma</s>, the southern direction, the autumn season, and as pertaining to the self — the mind, knowledge, and the knowable as the sense faculties.

children.text: tasya makāraśrutyetihāsapurāṇaṃ vāko vākyagāthānārāśaṃsīr upaniṣado 'nuśāsanānām iti vṛdhat karadguhan mahat tac cham o3m iti vyāhṛtīḥ svaraśamyanānātantrīḥ svaranṛtyagītavāditrāṇy anvabhavac caitrarathaṃ daivataṃ vaidyutaṃ jyotir vār hataṃ chandas tṛṇavat trayastriṃśau stomau dhruvām ūrdhvāṃ diśaṃ hemantaśiśirāv ṛtū śrotram adhyātmaṃ śabdaśravaṇam itīndriyāṇy anvabhavat // GpBr_1,1.21 //
children.translated_text: By the measure of the letter 'ma' — the scripture (<s>śruti</s>), <s>itihāsa</s> (epic narrative), <s>purāṇa</s> (ancient lore), speech-utterances, sentences, songs (<s>gāthā</s>), invocations (<s>nārāśaṃsī</s>), <s>Upaniṣad</s>s, and injunctions; and [the <s>vyāhṛti</s>s] '<s>vṛdhat</s>,' '<s>karad</s>,' '<s>guhan</s>,' '<s>mahat</s>,' '<s>tat</s>,' '<s>śam</s>,' 'Oṃ'; and the vowel-measured strings of the [musical] instrument; and the vowel-measured dance, song, and musical instruments — he experienced. [He experienced] the <s>Caitraratha</s> as the deity, the lightning as the radiance, the rain-song as the meter, the grass-like [rite], the <s>Trayastriṃśa</s> <s>stoma</s>, the fixed upward direction, the winter and dewy seasons, and as pertaining to the self — the ear, and the hearing of sound as the sense faculties.

children.text: saiṣaivākṣara ṛg brahmaṇas tapaso 'gre prādurbabhūva brahma vedasyātharvaṇaṃ śukram ata eva mantrāḥ prādurbabhūvuḥ sa tu khalu mantrāṇām atapasāśuśrūṣānadhyāyādhyayanena yad ūnaṃ ca viriṣṭaṃ ca yātayāmaṃ ca karoti tadatharvaṇāṃ tejasā pratyāpyāyayen mantrāś ca mām abhimukhībhaveyur garbhā iva mātaram abhijighāṃsuḥ purastād oṃkāraṃ prayuṅkta etayaiva tad ṛcā pratyāpyāyayed eṣaiva yajñasya purastād yujyata eṣā paścāt sarvata etayā yajñas tāyate / tad apy etad ṛcoktam / yā purastād yujyata ṛco 'kṣare parame vyomann iti / tad etad akṣaraṃ brāhmaṇo yaṃ kāmam icchet trirātropoṣitaḥ prāṅmukho vāgyato barhiṣy upaviśya sahasrakṛtvā āvartayet siddhanty asyārthāḥ sarvakarmāṇi ceti brāhmaṇam // GpBr_1,1.22 //
children.translated_text: This very syllable, the <s>Ṛc</s> (sacred verse), manifested at the beginning from the <s>tapas</s> (austerity) of <s>Brahman</s> — the <s>Brahman</s>, the bright seed (<s>śukra</s>) of the <s>Veda</s>, belonging to <s>Atharvan</s>. From that indeed the <s>mantra</s>s manifested. Now, whatever deficiency, excess, or spoilage one makes in the <s>mantra</s>s due to lack of austerity, lack of service, non-study, or non-recitation — one should revivify that by the power of the <s>Atharvan</s> [syllable], and [think:] 'May the <s>mantra</s>s turn toward me, like fetuses toward the mother.' Wishing to strike [the error], one should employ the <s>Oṃkāra</s> at the beginning; by this very <s>Ṛc</s> one should revivify [the mantras]. This very [syllable] is yoked at the beginning of the sacrifice; this at the end; [it pervades] everywhere. By this the sacrifice is extended. As this is stated by the <s>Ṛc</s>: 'That which is yoked at the beginning of the <s>Ṛc</s>, in the supreme, imperishable space.' This syllable — a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who desires any wish, having fasted for three nights, facing east, observing silence, sitting upon sacred grass, should repeat it a thousand times; his purposes and all his rites are accomplished — thus [says] the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [text].

children.text: vasorddhārāṇām aindranagarantadasurarāḥ paryavārayanta te devā bhītā āsan ka imān asurān apahaniṣyatīti ta oṃkāraṃ brahmaṇaḥ putraṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ dadṛśus te tam abruvan bhavatā mukhenemān asurān jayemeti / sa hovāca kiṃ me pratīvāho bhaviṣyatīti varaṃ vṛṇīṣyeti vṛṇā iti sa varam avṛṇīta na mām anīrayitvā brāhmaṇā brahma vadeyur yadi vadeyur abrahma tat syād iti tatheti te devā devayajanasyottarārdhe 'suraiḥ saṃyatā āsaṃs tān oṃkāreṇāgnīdhrīyād devā asurān parābhāvayanta tad yat parābhāvayanta tasmād oṃkāraḥ pūrva ucyate / yo ha vā etam oṃkāraṃ na vedāvaśaḥ syād ity atha ya eva veda brahma vaśaḥ syād iti tasmād oṃkāra ṛgy ṛg bhavati yajuṣi yajuḥ sāmni sāma sūtre sūtraṃ brāhmaṇe brāhmaṇaṃ śloke ślokaḥ praṇave praṇava iti brāhmaṇam // GpBr_1,1.23 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Asuras</s> surrounded [the gods] at the stream-channels of <s>Vasu</s>, at <s>Indra</s>'s city. The gods were frightened [and asked]: 'Who will strike down these <s>Asuras</s>?' They beheld <s>Oṃkāra</s>, the eldest son of <s>Brahman</s>. They said to him: 'With you at our head, let us conquer these <s>Asuras</s>.' He said: 'What will be my reward?' 'Choose a boon.' 'I choose,' [he said]. He chose this boon: '<s>Brāhmaṇas</s> should not utter <s>Brahman</s> [the Veda] without first uttering me; if they were to utter [it without me], that would be non-<s>Brahman</s>.' 'So be it.' The gods, joined in battle with the <s>Asuras</s> in the northern half of the place of sacrifice, defeated the <s>Asuras</s> with the <s>Oṃkāra</s> at the <s>Āgnīdhrīya</s> [fire]. Because they defeated [them], therefore <s>Oṃkāra</s> is uttered first. He who does not know this <s>Oṃkāra</s> would be powerless; but he who knows it would be master of <s>Brahman</s>. Therefore <s>Oṃkāra</s> in the <s>Ṛgveda</s> becomes an <s>ṛc</s>; in the <s>Yajurveda</s>, a <s>yajus</s>; in the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, a <s>sāman</s>; in a <s>sūtra</s>, a <s>sūtra</s>; in a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>; in a verse, a verse; in the <s>praṇava</s>, the <s>praṇava</s>. Thus [says] the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. (GpBr 1,1.23)

children.text: oṃkāraṃ pṛcchāmaḥ ko dhātuḥ kiṃ prātipadikaṃ kiṃ nāmākhyātaṃ kiṃ liṅgaṃ kiṃ vacanaṃ kā vibhaktiḥ kaḥ pratyayaḥ kaḥ svara upasargo nipātaḥ kiṃ vai vyākaraṇaṃ ko vikāraḥ ko vikārī katimātraḥ kativarṇaḥ katyakṣaraḥ katipadaḥ kaḥ saṃyogaḥ kiṃ sthānānupradānakaraṇaṃ śikṣukāḥ kim uccārayanti kiṃ chandaḥ ko varṇa iti pūrve praśnā athottare mantraḥ kalpo brāhmaṇam ṛgyajuḥ sāma kasmād brahmavādina oṃkāram āditaḥ kurvanti kiṃ devataṃ kiṃ jyotiṣaṃ kiṃ niruktaṃ kiṃ sthānaṃ kā prakṛtiḥ kim adhyātmam iti ṣaṭtriṃśat praśnāḥ pūrvottarāṇāṃ trayo vargā dvādaśakā etair oṃkāraṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ // GpBr_1,1.24 //
children.translated_text: We inquire about <s>Oṃkāra</s>: What is its root (<s>dhātu</s>)? What is its nominal stem (<s>prātipadika</s>)? Is it a noun or a verb (<s>nāmākhyāta</s>)? What is its gender (<s>liṅga</s>)? What is its number (<s>vacana</s>)? What is its case (<s>vibhakti</s>)? What is its suffix (<s>pratyaya</s>)? What is its accent (<s>svara</s>)? [Is it] a prefix (<s>upasarga</s>) or a particle (<s>nipāta</s>)? What indeed is its grammar (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>)? What is its modification (<s>vikāra</s>)? What is its modifier (<s>vikārin</s>)? How many measures (<s>mātrā</s>) does it have? How many sounds (<s>varṇa</s>)? How many syllables (<s>akṣara</s>)? How many words (<s>pada</s>)? What is its conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>)? What are its place of articulation, effort, and organ (<s>sthāna</s>, <s>anupradāna</s>, <s>karaṇa</s>)? How do students of phonetics (<s>śikṣā</s>) pronounce it? What is its meter (<s>chandas</s>)? What is its sound? — These are the first questions. And the latter ones: [What is its] mantra? [Its] ritual application (<s>kalpa</s>)? [Its] <s>brāhmaṇa</s> [explanation]? <s>Ṛc</s>, <s>yajus</s>, <s>sāman</s>? Why do speakers of <s>Brahman</s> place <s>Oṃkāra</s> at the beginning? What is its deity? What is its astronomy (<s>jyotiṣa</s>)? What is its etymology (<s>nirukta</s>)? What is its abode? What is its primal nature (<s>prakṛti</s>)? What is it in relation to the Self (<s>adhyātma</s>)? — These are the thirty-six questions, of the first and latter [sets], in three groups of twelve. By these we shall explain the <s>Oṃkāra</s>. (GpBr 1,1.24)

children.text: indraḥ prajāpatim apṛcchad bhagavann abhisūya pṛcchāmīti pṛccha vatsety abravīt kim ayam oṃkāraḥ kasya putraḥ kiṃ caitac chandaḥ kiṃ caitadvarṇaḥ kiṃcaitad brahmā brahma sampadyate tasmād vai tadbhadram oṃkāraṃ pūrvam ālebhe svaritodātta ekākṣara oṃkāra ṛgvede traisvaryodātta ekākṣara oṃkāro yajurvede dīrghaplutodātta ekākṣara oṃkāraḥ sāmavede hrasvodātta ekākṣara oṃkāro 'tharvaveda udāttodāttadvipada a u ity ardhacatasro mātrā makāre vyañjanam ity āhur yā sā prathamā mātrā brahmadevatyā raktā varṇena yas tāṃ dhyāyate nityaṃ sa gacched brāhmyaṃ padaṃ yā sā dvitīyā mātrā viṣṇudevatyā kṛṣṇā varṇena yas tāṃ dhyāyate nityaṃ sa gacched vaiṣṇavaṃ padaṃ yā sā tṛtīyā mātraiśānadevatyā kapilā varṇena yas tāṃ dhyāyate nityaṃ sa gacched aiśānaṃ padaṃ yā sārdhacaturthī mātrā sarvadevatyā vyaktībhūtā khaṃ vicarati śuddhasphaṭikasaṃnibhā varṇena yas tāṃ dhyāyate nityaṃ sa gacchet padam anāmakam oṃkārasya cotpattir vipro yo na jānāti tat punar upanayanaṃ tasmād brāhmaṇavacanam ādartavyaṃ yathā lātavyo gotro brahmaṇaḥ putro gāyatraṃ chandaḥ śuklo varṇaḥ puṃso vatso rudro devatā oṃkāro vedānām // GpBr_1,1.25 //
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> asked <s>Prajāpati</s>: 'Blessed one, I ask with reverence.' 'Ask, my child,' he replied. 'What is this <s>Oṃkāra</s>? Whose son is it? What is its meter? What is its sound? What is this <s>Brahman</s>?' <s>Brahman</s> is attained [through it]; therefore that auspicious <s>Oṃkāra</s> was first received. The <s>Oṃkāra</s> in the <s>Ṛgveda</s> is single-syllabled with the <s>svarita-udātta</s> accent; the <s>Oṃkāra</s> in the <s>Yajurveda</s> is single-syllabled with the <s>traisvarya-udātta</s> accent; the <s>Oṃkāra</s> in the <s>Sāmaveda</s> is single-syllabled with the prolonged <s>pluta-udātta</s> accent; the <s>Oṃkāra</s> in the <s>Atharvaveda</s> is single-syllabled with the short <s>udātta</s> accent. <s>Udātta-udātta</s>, two-footed. 'A' and 'U' — these are three-and-a-half <s>mātrā</s>s (measures); the <s>makāra</s> is a consonant, they say. The first <s>mātrā</s> has <s>Brahman</s> as its deity, is red in color; whoever meditates on it constantly reaches the station of <s>Brahman</s>. The second <s>mātrā</s> has <s>Viṣṇu</s> as its deity, is dark in color; whoever meditates on it constantly reaches the station of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. The third <s>mātrā</s> has <s>Īśāna</s> as its deity, is tawny in color; whoever meditates on it constantly reaches the station of <s>Īśāna</s>. The three-and-a-half <s>mātrā</s>, having all deities, having become manifest, wanders in space, resembling pure crystal in color; whoever meditates on it constantly reaches the nameless station. A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who does not know the origin of <s>Oṃkāra</s> — for him, the initiation (<s>upanayana</s>) should be performed again. Therefore, the word of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should be heeded. Thus: <s>Lātavya</s> by <s>gotra</s>, son of <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Gāyatra</s> by meter, white in color, a male calf, <s>Rudra</s> as deity — [such is] <s>Oṃkāra</s> of the <s>Vedas</s>. (GpBr 1,1.25)

children.text: ko dhātur ity āpṛr dhātur avatim apy eke rūpasāmānyād arthasāmānyanedīyas tasmād āper oṃkāraḥ sarvam āpnotīty arthaḥ kṛdantam arthavat prātipadikam adarśanaṃ pratyayasya nāma sampadyate nipāteṣu cainaṃ vaiyākaraṇā udāttaṃ samāmananti tad avyayībhūtam anvarthavācī śabdo na vyeti kadācaneti / sadṛśaṃ triṣu liṅgeṣu sarvāsu ca vibhaktiṣu / vacaneṣu ca sarveṣu yan na vyeti tad avyayam / ko vikārī cyavate prasāraṇam āptotirāva ā pakārī vikāryāvādita oṃkāro vikriyate dvitīyo makāra eva dvivarṇa ekākṣara oṃ ity oṃkāro nirvṛtaḥ // GpBr_1,1.26 //
children.translated_text: What is the root? [It is from] the root '<s>āp</s>' (to obtain); '<s>avat</s>' [is another form] according to some, due to the similarity of form, [but] the similarity of meaning is closer. Therefore, '<s>Oṃ</s>' [derives] from '<s>āp</s>' — the meaning is 'it obtains all.' A word ending in a <s>kṛt</s>-suffix that is meaningful [constitutes] a <s>prātipadika</s> (nominal stem). When the suffix is not visible, it becomes a name. The grammarians recite it among the indeclinables (<s>nipāta</s>) as having an acute (<s>udātta</s>) accent. That [which is] an indeclinable (<s>avyayībhūta</s>) — a word whose meaning accords [with its form] — never changes. 'That which is identical in the three genders, in all case-endings, and in all numbers, [and] which does not change — that is an indeclinable.' What undergoes modification? The spreading (<s>prasāraṇa</s>) — [the vowel] 'ā' changes; the first element, the '<s>o</s>' sound, is the modified [form] of <s>Oṃkāra</s>. The second element is the '<s>m</s>' sound alone. Of two phonemes and one syllable — thus <s>Oṃ</s>, the <s>Oṃkāra</s>, is accomplished. (GpBr 1.1.26)

children.text: katimātra ityādes tisro mātrā abhyādāne hi plavate makāraś caturthīṃ kiṃ sthānam ity ubhāv oṣṭhau sthānaṃ nādānupradānakaraṇau ca dvayasthānaṃ saṃdhyakṣaram avarṇaleśaḥ kaṇṭhyo yathoktaśeṣaḥ pūrvo vivṛtakaraṇasthitaś ca dvitīyaspṛṣṭakaraṇasthitaś ca na saṃyogo vidyūta ākhyātopasargānudāttasvaritaliṅgavibhaktivacanāni ca saṃsthānādhyāyina ācāryāḥ pūrve babhūvuḥ śravaṇād eva pratipadyante nakāraṇaṃ pṛcchanty athāparapakṣīyāṇāṃ kaviḥ pañcālacaṇḍaḥ paripṛcchako babhūvāṃ vu pṛthag udgīthadoṣān bhavanto bruvantv iti tad vāpy upalakṣayed varṇākṣarapadāṅkaśo vibhaktyām ṛṣiniṣevitām iti vācaṃ stuvanti tasmāt kāraṇaṃ brūmo varṇānām ayam idaṃ bhaviṣyatīti ṣaḍaṅgavidas tat tathādhīmahe / kiṃ chanda iti gāyatraṃ hi chando gāyatrī vai devānām ekākṣarā śvetavarṇā ca vyākhyātā dvau dvādaśakau vargāv etad vai vyākaraṇaṃ dhātvarthavacanaṃ śaikṣyaṃ chandovacanaṃ cāthottarau dvau dvādaśakau vargau vedarahasikī vyākhyātā mantraḥ kalpo brāhmaṇam ṛg yajuḥ sāmātharvāṇy eṣā vyāhṛtiś caturṇāṃ vedānām ānupūrveṇoṃ bhūr bhuvasvar iti vyāhṛtayaḥ // GpBr_1,1.27 //
children.translated_text: How many <s>mātrās</s> (metrical units)? Three <s>mātrās</s> initially, for the '<s>m</s>' sound floats [as a fourth] when prolonged. What is the place of articulation? Both lips are the place of articulation; <s>nāda</s> (resonance) and complementary effort are the instruments. It has a dual place of articulation; it is a <s>saṃdhyakṣara</s> (conjunction-syllable), with a trace of the '<s>a</s>'-vowel; the guttural [element arises] as described; the first [element] is in the open articulation position, while the second is in the closed articulation position. There is no conjunction [of consonants]. [The grammatical categories of] <s>ākhyāta</s> (verb), <s>upasarga</s> (prefix), <s>anudātta</s> (grave accent), <s>svarita</s> (circumflex), gender, case, and number — the earlier teachers who studied the system (<s>saṃsthānādhyāyin</s>) understood these through hearing alone. They did not ask 'why?' But among the opposing school, the poet <s>Pañcāla-Caṇḍa</s> was the questioner. He said: 'Let the honored ones declare the defects of the <s>Udgītha</s> (chanting) separately.' One should observe that by phoneme, syllable, word, and number, in the declension practiced by the <s>ṛṣis</s> — they praise Speech. Therefore we state the reason: 'This phoneme will become this' — those who know the six <s>Vedāṅgas</s> (auxiliary sciences of the Veda) [say thus]. We study it accordingly. What is the meter? <s>Gāyatra</s> indeed is the meter. <s>Gāyatrī</s> is the one-syllabled [meter] of the gods, explained as having a white color. Two groups of twelve — this indeed is grammar (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>): the statement of root-meanings and phonetics (<s>śikṣā</s>), and the statement of meters (<s>chandas</s>). The latter two groups of twelve are the esoteric [interpretation of the] <s>Veda</s>: <s>mantra</s>, <s>kalpa</s> (ritual procedure), <s>brāhmaṇa</s> (prose commentary), <s>Ṛk</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, <s>Sāman</s>, and <s>Atharvan</s>. This is the <s>vyāhṛti</s> (sacred utterance) of the four <s>Vedas</s>, in order: '<s>Oṃ Bhūr Bhuvas Svaḥ</s>' — [these are] the <s>vyāhṛtis</s>. (GpBr 1.1.27)

children.text: asamīkṣapravahlitāni śrūyante dvāparādāv ṛṣīṇām ekadeśo doṣapatir iha cintām āpede tribhiḥ somaḥ pātavyaḥ samāptam iva bhavati tasmād ṛgyajuḥsāmāny apakrāntatejāṃsy āsaṃs tatra maharṣayaḥ paridevayāṃcakrire mahac chokabhayaṃ prāptāsmo na caitat sarvaiḥ samabhihitaṃ te vayaṃ bhagavantam evopadhāvāma sarveṣām eva śarma bhavānīti te tathety uktvā tūṣṇīm atiṣṭhan nānupasannebhya ity upopasīdāmīti nīcair babhūvuḥ / sa ebhya upanīya provāca māmikām eva vyāhṛtim āditaḥ āditaḥ kṛṇudhvam ity evaṃ māmakā ādhīyante / narte bhṛgvaṅgirovidbhyaḥ somaḥ pātavya ṛtvijaḥ parābhavanti yajamāno rajasāpadhyasyati śrutiś cāpadhyastā tiṣṭhatīty evam evottarottarād yogāt tokaṃ tokam praśādhvam ity evaṃ pratāpo na parābhaviṣyatīti tathāha tathāha bhagavann iti pratipedira āpyāyayaṃs te tathā vītaśokabhayā babhūvuḥ / tasmād brahmavādina oṃkāram āditaḥ kurvanti // GpBr_1,1.28 //
children.translated_text: Utterances made without proper examination are heard [to have occurred] at the beginning of the <s>Dvāpara</s> [age]. A partial lord of faults among the <s>ṛṣis</s> fell into anxiety here [thinking]: '<s>Soma</s> must be drunk with [all] three [Vedas]; it seems to be completed.' Therefore the <s>Ṛk</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāman</s> [Vedas] had their splendor diminished. Thereupon the great sages lamented: 'We have come upon a great sorrow and fear. This has not been properly articulated by all [of us]. Let us indeed resort to the Blessed One himself. May he be the shelter for all of us.' Having said 'So be it,' they stood in silence — [thinking] 'one should not [teach] to those who have not approached [as students],' [so] 'let us approach as students.' They became humble. He, having initiated them, declared: 'Place my <s>vyāhṛti</s> (sacred utterance) at the very beginning, at the very beginning!' Thus those belonging to me [i.e., the Atharvan tradition] are studied [first]. 'Without <s>Soma</s> being drunk by those who know <s>Bhṛgu</s> and <s>Aṅgiras</s>, the priests (<s>ṛtvij</s>) fail; the sacrificer (<s>yajamāna</s>) sinks into darkness; and the revealed scripture (<s>śruti</s>) too, though sunk, stands [firm].' 'Thus from each successive connection, protect generation after generation.' 'In this way, splendor will not fail.' 'So it is, so it is, O Blessed One!' — thus they accepted. They were filled; thus they became free from sorrow and fear. Therefore, those who discourse on <s>Brahman</s> place <s>Oṃkāra</s> at the very beginning. (GpBr 1.1.28)

children.text: kiṃdevatam ity ṛcām agnir devataṃ tad eva jyotir gāyatraṃ chandaḥ pṛthivī sthānam / agnim īḍe purohitaṃ yajñasya devam ṛtvijam / hotāraṃ ratnadhātamam ity evam ādiṃ kṛtvā ṛgvedam adhīyate / yajuṣāṃ vāyur devataṃ tad eva jyotiḥ traiṣṭubhaṃ chando 'ntarikṣaṃ sthānam / ikhe tv orje tvā vāyava stha devo vaḥ savitā prārpayatu / śreṣṭhatamāya karmaṇa ity evam ādiṃ kṛtvā yajurvedam adhīyate / sāmnām ādityo devataṃ tad eva jyotir jāgataṃ chando dyau sthānam / agna āyāhi vītaye gṛṇāno havyadātaye / nihotā satsi barhiṣīty evam ādiṃ kṛtvā sāmavedam adhīyate / atharvaṇāṃ candramā devataṃ tad eva jyotiḥ sarvāṇi chandāṃsy āpaḥ sthānam / śanno deve rabhiṣṭa ya ity evam ādiṃ kṛtvā atharvavedam adhīyate / adbhyaḥ sthāvarajaṅgamo bhūtagrāmaḥ sambhavati tasmāt sarvam āpomayaṃ bhūtaṃ sarvaṃ bhṛgvaṅgiromayam / antaraite trayo vedā bhṛgūn aṅgirasaḥ śritā ity ab iti prakṛtir apām oṃkāreṇa caitasmād vyāsaḥ purovāca bhṛgvaṅgirovidā saṃskṛto 'nyān vedān adhīyīta nānyatra saṃskṛto bhṛgvaṅgiraso 'dhīyīta atha sāmavede khilaśrutiḥ brahmacaryeṇa caitasmād atharvāṅgiraso ha yo vedaḥ sa veda sarvam iti brāhmaṇam // GpBr_1,1.29 //
children.translated_text: What is the deity? Of the <s>Ṛc</s>-verses, <s>Agni</s> is the deity, that itself is the light, the <s>Gāyatrī</s> is the meter, and the earth is the abode. 'I praise <s>Agni</s>, the <s>purohita</s> (household priest), the god of the sacrifice, the <s>ṛtvij</s> (officiant), the <s>hotṛ</s> (invoker), the best bestower of treasures'—beginning with this, one studies the <s>Ṛgveda</s>. Of the <s>Yajus</s> (-formulae), <s>Vāyu</s> is the deity, that itself is the light, the <s>Traiṣṭubha</s> is the meter, and the atmosphere is the abode. 'For sap, for vitality—you are [the offerings] for <s>Vāyu</s>; may the god <s>Savitṛ</s> impel you to the most excellent rite'—beginning with this, one studies the <s>Yajurveda</s>. Of the <s>Sāmans</s> (chants), <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun) is the deity, that itself is the light, the <s>Jāgata</s> is the meter, and heaven is the abode. 'O <s>Agni</s>, come to the feast, praised one, to the giving of offerings; sit as the <s>hotṛ</s> upon the sacred grass'—beginning with this, one studies the <s>Sāmaveda</s>. Of the <s>Atharvan</s>-[hymns], the Moon (<s>Candramās</s>) is the deity, that itself is the light, all meters [apply], and the waters are the abode. 'May the divine god (<s>Deva</s>) be propitious to us'—beginning with this, one studies the <s>Atharvaveda</s>. From the waters the entire community of beings, both stationary and mobile, comes into being; therefore all being is made of water, all is made of <s>Bhṛgu</s> and <s>Aṅgiras</s>. 'Within these three <s>Vedas</s>, the <s>Bhṛgus</s> and <s>Aṅgirasas</s> are established.' <s>Ab</s> is the root-form (<s>prakṛti</s>) of the waters. With the <s>Oṃkāra</s>, and from this, <s>Vyāsa</s> declared formerly: 'One consecrated (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) by the <s>Bhṛgvaṅgiras</s> [Veda] should study the other <s>Vedas</s>; one not thus consecrated should not study the <s>Bhṛgvaṅgiras</s> [Veda].' Moreover, in the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, there is a supplementary scripture (<s>khilaśruti</s>): 'Through <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate studentship) in this [Veda], whoever knows the <s>Atharvāṅgiras</s> <s>Veda</s>—he knows everything'—thus [says] the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. // GpBr_1,1.29 //

children.text: adhyātmam ātmabhaiṣajyam ātmakaivalyam oṃkāra ātmānaṃ nirudhya saṅgam amātrīṃ bhūtārthacintāṃ cintayed atikramya vedebhyaḥ sarvaparamādhyātmaphalaṃ prāpnotīty arthaḥ savitarkaṃ jñānam ayam ity etaiḥ praśnaiḥ prativacanaiś ca yathārthaṃ padam anuvicintya prakaraṇajño hi prabalo viṣayī syāt sarvasmin vāko vākya iti brāhmaṇam // GpBr_1,1.30 //
children.translated_text: Pertaining to the self (<s>adhyātma</s>): [this is] the self's medicine (<s>ātmabhaiṣajya</s>), the self's sole liberation (<s>ātmakaivalya</s>). Through the <s>Oṃkāra</s>, restraining the self, [abandoning] attachment, [and] the measureless contemplation of the reality of beings—one should meditate. Transcending the <s>Vedas</s>, one obtains the supreme fruit pertaining to the self (<s>adhyātma</s>)—this is the meaning. Knowledge accompanied by reasoning (<s>savitarka</s>)—this [is expressed] through these questions and answers. Having contemplated the true meaning word by word, for one who knows the context becomes a powerful master of the subject—in all utterances, word by word—thus [says] the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. // GpBr_1,1.30 //

children.text: etaddha smaitad vidvāṃsam ekādaśākṣam maudgalyaṃ glāvo maitre yo 'bhyājagāma sa tasmin brahmacaryaṃ vasato vijñāyovāca kiṃ svinmaryā ayaṃ taṃ maudgalyo 'dhyeti yad asmin brahmacarye vasatīti taddhi maudgalyasyāntevāsī śuśrāva saḥ ācāryāyāvrajyācacaṣṭe duradhīyānaṃ vā ayaṃ bhavantam avocad yo 'yam adyātithir bhavati kiṃ saumya vidvān iti / trīn vedān brūte bho 3 iti tasya saumya yo vispaṣṭo vijigīṣo 'ntevāsī tan me hvayeti tam ājuhāva tam abhyuvācāsāv iti bho 3 iti kiṃ saumya ta ācāryo 'dhyetīti trīn vedān brūte bho 3 iti yan nu khalu saumyāsmābhiḥ sarve vedā mukhato gṛhītāḥ kathaṃ ta evam ācāryo bhāṣate kathaṃ nu śiṣṭāḥ śiṣṭebhya evaṃ bhāṣeran yaṃ hy enam ahaṃ praśnaṃ pracchāmi na taṃ vivakṣyati na hy enam adhyetīti / sa ha maudgalyaḥ svam antevāsinam uvāca parehi saumya glāvaṃ maitreyam upasīdādhīhi bho sāvitrīṃ gāyatrīṃ caturviṃśatiyoniṃ dvādaśamithunāṃ yasyā bhṛgvaṅgirasaś cakṣur yasyāṃ sarvam idaṃ śritaṃ tāṃ bhavān prabravītv iti sa cet saumya duradhīyāno bhaviṣyaty ācāryovāca brahmacārī brahmacāriṇe sāvitrīṃ prāheti vakṣyati tattvaṃ brūyāt duradhīyānaṃ taṃ vai bhavān maudgalyam avocat sa tvā yaṃ praśnam aprākṣīn na taṃ vyavocaḥ purā saṃvatsarād ārtim ākṛṣyasīti // GpBr_1,1.31 //
children.translated_text: This indeed is [what happened]: <s>Glāva Maitreya</s>, knowing [the reputation of] the learned <s>Maudgalya</s> of eleven syllables (<s>Ekādaśākṣa</s>), approached him. As he was dwelling there observing <s>brahmacarya</s>, [<s>Maudgalya</s>], having recognized [him], said: 'Why does this young man study with this <s>Maudgalya</s>, that he dwells in this state of <s>brahmacarya</s>?' When an inner student of <s>Maudgalya</s> heard this, he went to the teacher and reported: 'This guest who is present today has called you poorly taught. What does [he] know, good sir?' 'He says he knows three <s>Vedas</s>, sir.' 'Good sir, [summon] that student of his who is prominent and competitive—call him to me.' He summoned him. [<s>Maudgalya</s>] addressed him: 'So-and-so—sir!' 'What, good sir, does your teacher study?' 'He says [he knows] three <s>Vedas</s>, sir.' 'But good sir, all the <s>Vedas</s> have been received by us from memory. How then does your teacher speak thus? How could the learned speak thus to the learned? For the question I ask him, he will not be able to answer—he does not [truly] study it.' Then <s>Maudgalya</s> said to his own student: 'Go, good sir, approach <s>Glāva Maitreya</s>. Study, sir, the <s>Sāvitrī Gāyatrī</s>, having twenty-four origins, twelve pairs, whose eye is the <s>Bhṛgvaṅgiras</s> [Veda], in which all this is established—may you expound that.' 'If, good sir, he should say you are poorly taught,' the teacher said, 'he will say: "A <s>brahmacārin</s> (student) teaches the <s>Sāvitrī</s> to a <s>brahmacārin</s>." You should tell the truth: "You indeed called that <s>Maudgalya</s> poorly taught. He [then] asked you a question that you could not answer. Before a year [passes], you will bring suffering upon yourself."' // GpBr_1,1.31 //

children.text: sa tatrājagāma yatretaro babhūva taṃ ha papraccha sa ha na pratipede taṃ hovāca duradhīyānaṃ taṃ vai bhavān maudgalyam avocat sa tvā yaṃ praśnam aprākṣīn na taṃ vyavocaḥ purā saṃvatsarād ārtim ākṛṣyasīti / sa ha maitreyaḥ svān antevāsina uvāca yathārthaṃ bhavanto yathāgṛhaṃ yathāmano viprasṛjyantāṃ duradhīyānaṃ vā ahaṃ maudgalyam avocaṃ sa mā yaṃ praśnam aprākṣīn na taṃ vyavocaṃ tam upeṣyāmi śāntiṃ kariṣyāmīti / saha maitreyaḥ prātaḥ samitpāṇir maudgalyam upasasādāsāv āgrahaṃ bho maitreyaḥ kim artham iti duradhīyānaṃ vā ahaṃ bhavantam avocaṃ tvaṃ mā yam praśnam aprākṣīr na taṃ vyavocaṃ tvām upeṣyāmi śāntiṃ kariṣyāmīti sa hovācātra vā upetaṃ ca sarvaṃ ca kṛtaṃ pāpakena tvā yānena carantam āhvaratho 'yaṃ mama kalyāṇas taṃ te dadāmi tena yāhīti / sa hovācaitad evātrātviṣaṃ cānṛśaṃsyaṃ ca yathā bhavān āhopāyām ity eva bhavantam iti taṃ hopeyāya taṃ hopetya papraccha kiṃ svid āhur bhoḥ savitur vareṇyaṃ bhargo devasya kavayaḥ kim āhur dhiyo vicakṣva yadi tāḥ praveptya pracodayāṃt savitā yābhir etīti / tasmā etat provāca vedāś chandāṃsi savitur vareṇyaṃ bhargo devasya kavayo 'nnam āhuḥ / karmāṇi dhiyas tad u te bravīmi pracodayāṃt savitā yābhir etīti / tam upasaṃgṛhya papracchādhīhi bhoḥ kaḥ savitā kā sāvitrī // GpBr_1,1.32 //
children.translated_text: He went to where the other one was and asked him, but he did not understand. He said to him: 'You have called <s>Maudgalya</s> difficult to teach. He asked you a question and you did not answer it. Before a year [passes], you will bring affliction upon yourself.' Then <s>Maitreya</s> said to his own students: 'Let the venerable ones disperse to their homes, to their families, as they wish, for I have indeed called <s>Maudgalya</s> difficult to teach. He asked me a question and I did not answer it. I shall approach him and make amends.' <s>Maitreya</s>, with fuel-sticks in hand, approached <s>Maudgalya</s> in the morning. 'Here I am, sir.' 'O <s>Maitreya</s>, for what purpose?' 'I have indeed called you difficult to teach. You asked me a question and I did not answer it. I shall approach you [as a student] and make amends.' He said: 'Here, approach and all is done. You were going about in a wicked vehicle, and I called you. Now, this auspicious [vehicle] of mine — I give it to you; go with it.' He replied: 'This very thing was disagreeable to me — the unkindness — that you, sir, [said]. Let me approach you as a student.' 'Very well,' [said <s>Maudgalya</s>]. He approached him, and having approached, he asked: 'What indeed do the wise ones (<s>kavayaḥ</s>) call the chosen splendor (<s>vareṇyaṃ bhargaḥ</s>) of the god <s>Savitṛ</s>? Reveal the thoughts (<s>dhiyaḥ</s>)! If those are to be experienced, may <s>Savitṛ</s> impel them — by which he proceeds.' He declared this to him: 'The <s>Vedas</s> and the meters (<s>chandāṃsi</s>) — the wise ones call them the chosen splendor of the god <s>Savitṛ</s>; food is [his splendor]. The thoughts are the ritual actions — this I tell you. May <s>Savitṛ</s> impel [those] by which he proceeds.' Having clasped his [feet], he asked: 'Teach me, sir! Who is <s>Savitṛ</s>? Who is <s>Sāvitrī</s>?' // GpBr 1,1.32 //

children.translated_text: The mind itself is <s>Savitṛ</s>; speech is <s>Sāvitrī</s>. Where there is mind, there is speech; where there is speech, there is mind — these are two wombs, one couple. <s>Agni</s> (fire) indeed is <s>Savitṛ</s>; <s>Pṛthivī</s> (earth) is <s>Sāvitrī</s>. Where there is fire, there is earth; where there is earth, there is fire — these are two wombs, one couple. <s>Vāyu</s> (wind) indeed is <s>Savitṛ</s>; <s>Antarikṣa</s> (atmosphere) is <s>Sāvitrī</s>. Where there is wind, there is the atmosphere; where there is the atmosphere, there is wind — these are two wombs, one couple. <s>Āditya</s> (the sun) indeed is <s>Savitṛ</s>; <s>Dyaus</s> (heaven) is <s>Sāvitrī</s>. Where there is the sun, there is heaven; where there is heaven, there is the sun — these are two wombs, one couple. <s>Candramās</s> (the moon) indeed is <s>Savitṛ</s>; the <s>nakṣatras</s> (constellations) are <s>Sāvitrī</s>. Where there is the moon, there are the constellations; where there are the constellations, there is the moon — these are two wombs, one couple. Day indeed is <s>Savitṛ</s>; night is <s>Sāvitrī</s>. Where there is day, there is night; where there is night, there is day — these are two wombs, one couple. Heat indeed is <s>Savitṛ</s>; cold is <s>Sāvitrī</s>. Where there is heat, there is cold; where there is cold, there is heat — these are two wombs, one couple. Cloud indeed is <s>Savitṛ</s>; rain is <s>Sāvitrī</s>. Where there is cloud, there is rain; where there is rain, there is cloud — these are two wombs, one couple. Lightning indeed is <s>Savitṛ</s>; thunder is <s>Sāvitrī</s>. Where there is lightning, there is thunder; where there is thunder, there is lightning — these are two wombs, one couple. <s>Prāṇa</s> (breath) indeed is <s>Savitṛ</s>; food is <s>Sāvitrī</s>. Where there is breath, there is food; where there is food, there is breath — these are two wombs, one couple. The <s>Vedas</s> indeed are <s>Savitṛ</s>; the meters (<s>chandāṃsi</s>) are <s>Sāvitrī</s>. Where there are the <s>Vedas</s>, there are the meters; where there are the meters, there are the <s>Vedas</s> — these are two wombs, one couple. The sacrifice (<s>yajña</s>) indeed is <s>Savitṛ</s>; the sacrificial fee (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) is <s>Sāvitrī</s>. Where there is sacrifice, there is the fee; where there is the fee, there is sacrifice — these are two wombs, one couple. Thus indeed the learned <s>Opākārimāsastur</s> [said to] a celibate student: 'These are set forth. These, though placed thus, have become as if unplaced. Now he departed to bathe.' 'This indeed I know — I who am born from these wombs, from these couples — no celibate student shall depart before me in full lifespan.' // GpBr 1,1.33 //

children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> indeed beheld prosperity, foundation, and abode for this [creation]. 'Perform austerity for that; may it be maintained in the vow.' That was established in truth. <s>Savitṛ</s> (the Impeller), having created the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> through the <s>Sāvitrī</s> [mantra], bestowed that <s>Sāvitrī</s> [upon him]. 'Tat savitur vareṇyam' ('That excellent [glory] of <s>Savitṛ</s>') — this is the first <s>pāda</s> (quarter) of the <s>Sāvitrī</s>. He conjoined it with the earth and the <s>Ṛc</s> (verse); with the <s>Ṛc</s>, <s>Agni</s> (fire); with <s>Agni</s>, prosperity; with prosperity, a wife; with a wife, a couple; with a couple, offspring; with offspring, ritual action; with action, austerity; with austerity, truth; with truth, <s>Brahman</s>; with <s>Brahman</s>, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>; with the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the vow. By the vow indeed the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> becomes sharpened; he becomes non-empty; he becomes unbroken; unbroken is his thread [of lineage]; unbroken is his life; his dwelling becomes [secure] — whoever knows this, and whoever, knowing thus, expounds this first <s>pāda</s> of the <s>Sāvitrī</s>.

He conjoined it with the atmosphere and the <s>Yajus</s> (sacrificial formula); with the <s>Yajus</s>, <s>Vāyu</s> (wind); with <s>Vāyu</s>, clouds; with clouds, rain; with rain, herbs and trees; with herbs and trees, cattle; with cattle, ritual action; with action, austerity; with austerity, truth; with truth, <s>Brahman</s>; with <s>Brahman</s>, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>; with the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the vow.
