children.translated_text: 'Dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayāt' ('May he inspire our thoughts') — this is the third <s>pāda</s> of the <s>Sāvitrī</s>. He conjoined it with heaven and the <s>Sāman</s> (chant); with the <s>Sāman</s>, <s>Āditya</s> (the sun); with <s>Āditya</s>, rays; with rays, rain; with rain, herbs and trees; with herbs and trees, cattle; with cattle, ritual action; with action, austerity; with austerity, truth; with truth, <s>Brahman</s>; with <s>Brahman</s>, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>; with the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the vow. By the vow indeed the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> becomes sharpened; he becomes non-empty; he becomes unbroken; unbroken is his thread; unbroken is his life — whoever knows this, and whoever, knowing thus, expounds this third <s>pāda</s> of the <s>Sāvitrī</s>.

children.text: tena ha vā evaṃ viduṣā brāhmaṇena brahmābhipannaṃ grasitaṃ parāmṛṣṭaṃ brahmaṇākāśam abhipannaṃ grasitaṃ parāmṛṣṭam ākāśena vāyur abhipanno grasitaḥ parāmṛṣṭo vāyunā jyotir abhipannaṃ grasitaṃ parāmṛṣṭaṃ jyotiṣāpo 'bhipannā grasitāḥ parāmṛṣṭā adbhir bhūmir abhipannā grasitā parāmṛṣṭā bhūmyānnam abhipannaṃ grasitaṃ parāmṛṣṭam annena prāṇo 'bhipanno grasitaḥ parāmṛṣṭaḥ prāṇena mano 'bhipannaṃ grasitaṃ parāmṛṣṭaṃ manasā vāg abhipannā grasitā parāmṛṣṭā vācā vedā abhipannā grasitāḥ parāmṛṣṭā vedair yajño 'bhipanno grasitaḥ parāmṛṣṭas tāni ha vā etāni dvādaśamahābhūtāny evaṃ vidhipratiṣṭhitāni teṣāṃ yajña eva parārdhyaḥ // GpBr_1,1.37 //
children.translated_text: By that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who knows thus, <s>Brahman</s> is encompassed, grasped, and seized. By <s>Brahman</s>, space (<s>ākāśa</s>) is encompassed, grasped, and seized. By space, wind (<s>vāyu</s>) is encompassed, grasped, and seized. By wind, light (<s>jyotis</s>) is encompassed, grasped, and seized. By light, the waters are encompassed, grasped, and seized. By the waters, the earth is encompassed, grasped, and seized. By the earth, food is encompassed, grasped, and seized. By food, the breath (<s>prāṇa</s>) is encompassed, grasped, and seized. By breath, the mind is encompassed, grasped, and seized. By the mind, speech is encompassed, grasped, and seized. By speech, the <s>Veda</s>s are encompassed, grasped, and seized. By the <s>Veda</s>s, the sacrifice (<s>yajña</s>) is encompassed, grasped, and seized. These indeed are the twelve great entities (<s>mahābhūta</s>s), established in this manner, of which the sacrifice is the highest.

children.text: te ha smaitam evaṃ vidvāṃso manyante vidmainam iti yāthātathyam avidvāṃso 'yaṃ yajño vedeṣu pratiṣṭhito vedā vāci pratiṣṭhitā vāṅ manasi pratiṣṭhitā manaḥ prāṇe pratiṣṭhitaṃ prāṇo 'nne pratiṣṭhito 'nnaṃ bhūmau pratiṣṭhitaṃ bhūmir apsu pratiṣṭhitā āpo jyotiṣi pratiṣṭhitā jyotir vāyau pratiṣṭhitaṃ vāyur ākāśe pratiṣṭhita ākāśaṃ brahmaṇi pratiṣṭhitaṃ brahma brāhmaṇe brahmavidi pratiṣṭhitaṃ yo ha vā evaṃ vit sa brahmavit puṇyāṃ ca kīrtiṃ labhate surabhīṃś ca gandhān so 'pahatapāpmānantyaśriyam aśnute ya evaṃ veda yaś caivaṃ vidvān evam etāṃ vedānāṃ mātaraṃ sāvitrīsampadam upaniṣadam upāsta iti brāhmaṇam // GpBr_1,1.38 //
children.translated_text: Those who knew this thus would think: 'We know him' — [but that is] in the true sense [only for those who truly know]; those who do not [truly] know [think:] 'This sacrifice is established in the <s>Veda</s>s; the <s>Veda</s>s are established in speech; speech is established in the mind; the mind is established in breath; breath is established in food; food is established in the earth; the earth is established in the waters; the waters are established in light; light is established in wind; wind is established in space; space is established in <s>Brahman</s>; <s>Brahman</s> is established in the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the knower of <s>Brahman</s>.' Whoever indeed knows thus — he is a knower of <s>Brahman</s>. He obtains auspicious fame and fragrant odors. He, with sin destroyed, attains endless prosperity — whoever knows this, and whoever, knowing thus, meditates upon (<s>upāste</s>) this <s>Upaniṣad</s>, the wealth of the <s>Sāvitrī</s>, the mother of the <s>Veda</s>s — thus [says] the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [text].

children.text:
āpo garbhaṃ janayantīr ity apāṅgarbhaḥ puruṣaḥ sa yajño 'dbhir yajñaḥ praṇīyamānaḥ prāṅṇāyate tasmād ācamanīyaṃ pūrvam āhārayati sa yadācāmati trir ācāmati dviḥ pariśumbhaty āyur avaruhya pāpmānaṃ nirṇudaty upasādya yajuṣoddhṛtya mantrān prayujyāvasāya prācīḥ śākhāḥ saṃdhāyonir aṅguṣṭhe pāṇāv amṛtam asya mṛtopastaraṇam asya mṛtāya tvopastṛṇāmīti pāṇāv udakam ānīya jīvāstheti sūktena trir ācāmati / sa yat pūrvam ācāmati sapta prāṇāṃs tān etenāsminn āpyāyayati yā hy emā vāhyāḥ śarīrān mātrās tad yathaitad agniṃ vāyum ādityaṃ candramasam apaḥ paśūn anyāṃś ca prajās tān etenāsminn āpyāyayaty āpo 'mṛtam / sa yad dvitīyam ācāmati saptāpānāṃs tān etenāsmin āpyāyayati yā hy emā vāhyāḥ śarīrān mātrās tad yathaitat paurṇamāsīm aṣṭakām amāvāsyāṃ śraddhāṃ dīkṣāṃ yajñaṃ dakṣiṇās tān etenāsminn āpyāyayaty āpo 'mṛtam / sa yat tṛtīyam ācāmati sapta vyānāṃs tān etenāsminn āpyāyayati yā hy emā vāhyāḥ śarīrān mātrās tad yathaitat pṛthivīm antarīkṣaṃ divannakṣatrāeyṛtūnārtavān saṃvatsarāṃs tān etenāsminn āpyāyayaty āpo 'mṛtaṃ puruṣo brahmāthāpriyanigamo bhavati tasmād vai vidvān puruṣam idaṃ puṇḍarīkam iti prāṇa eṣa sa puri śete saṃpuriśaṃta iti / puriśayaṃ santaṃ prāṇaṃ puruṣa ity ācakṣate / parokṣeṇa parokṣapriyā iva hi devā bhavanti pratyakṣadviṣaḥ / sa yat pūrvam ācāmati purastāddhomāṃs tenāsminn avarundhe sa yad dvitīyam ācāmaty ājyabhāgau tenāsminn avarundhe sa yat tṛtīyam ācāmati saṃsthitahomāṃs tenāsminn avarundhe sa yad dviḥ pariśumbhati tat samitsaṃbarhiḥ sa yat sarvāṇi khāni sarvaṃ deham āpyāyayati yac cānyad ātāraṃ mantrakāryaṃ yajñe skandati sarvaṃ tenāsminn avarundhe sa yad oṃpūrvān mantrān prayuṅkta
āsarvamedhād ete kratava eta evāsya sarveṣu lokeṣu sarveṣu deveṣu sarveṣu vedeṣu sarveṣu bhūteṣu sarveṣu sattveṣu kāmacāraḥ kāmavimocanaṃ bhavaty ardhe ca na pramīyate ya evaṃ veda / tad apy etad ṛcoktam / āpo bhṛgvaṅgirorūpam āpo bhṛgvaṅgiromayam / sarvam āpomayaṃ bhūtaṃ sarvaṃ bhṛgvaṅgiromayam / antaraite trayo vedā bhṛgūn aṅgiraso 'nugāḥ / apāṃ puṣpaṃ mūrtir ākāśaṃ pavitram uttamam ity ācamyābhyukṣyātmānam anumantrayata indra jīveti brāhmaṇam // GpBr_1,1.39 //
children.translated_text: 'The waters generating the embryo' — the embryo of the waters is the Person (<s>Puruṣa</s>); he is the sacrifice. The sacrifice, being led forward with waters, is brought forward. Therefore one first brings the sipping-water (<s>ācamanīya</s>). When he sips, he sips three times and purifies twice. Having descended upon life, he drives away sin. Having approached, having extracted with the <s>yajus</s>, having employed the mantras and concluded, having joined the eastern branches — the womb is in the thumb, in the palm is immortality, its spreading below is of the dead, 'I spread for you who are dead' — having brought water into the palm, with the hymn 'jīvā stha' (you are alive), he sips three times. When he sips the first time, the seven <s>prāṇa</s>s (vital breaths) — he nourishes them in himself by this. For those measures which are external to the body — just as fire, wind, the sun, the moon, the waters, cattle, and other creatures — he nourishes them in himself by this. Waters are immortality. When he sips the second time, the seven <s>apāna</s>s (downward breaths) — he nourishes them in himself by this. For those measures which are external to the body — just as the full-moon day, the eighth-day rite, the new-moon day, faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), consecration (<s>dīkṣā</s>), sacrifice, and the priestly fees (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) — he nourishes them in himself by this. Waters are immortality. When he sips the third time, the seven <s>vyāna</s>s (diffused breaths) — he nourishes them in himself by this. For those measures which are external to the body — just as the earth, the atmosphere, the sky, the constellations (<s>nakṣatra</s>), the seasons, the year-divisions, and the years — he nourishes them in himself by this. Waters are immortality. The Person is <s>Brahman</s>; then he becomes one whose understanding is dear. Therefore indeed the learned one [calls] this Person a 'lotus' (<s>puṇḍarīka</s>) — this breath (<s>prāṇa</s>), he sleeps in the city (<s>puri śete</s>); therefore 'Puriśaya.' They call the breath that sleeps in the city '<s>Puruṣa</s>' — by indirection, for the gods are fond of the indirect and averse to the direct. When he sips the first time, he secures in himself the preliminary oblations; when he sips the second time, he secures the <s>ājya</s>-portions (ghee-offerings); when he sips the third time, he secures the concluding oblations. When he purifies twice — that is the fuel and the sacrificial grass. When he nourishes all the openings [of the body] and the entire body — whatever other mantric operations of the sacrifice may be scattered, he secures all of them in himself. When he employs mantras preceded by Oṃ — [he attains benefits] up to the <s>Sarvamedha</s> (universal sacrifice). These are the rites; by these he has free movement in all worlds, among all gods, in all <s>Vedas</s>, among all beings, among all creatures — and freedom of release at will; and he does not die before the [allotted] half [of his life]. [He who] knows thus. And this too is stated in the <s>ṛc</s>: 'The waters are of the form of <s>Bhṛgu</s>s and <s>Aṅgiras</s>es; the waters are pervaded by <s>Bhṛgu</s>s and <s>Aṅgiras</s>es. All beings are pervaded by water; all is pervaded by <s>Bhṛgu</s>s and <s>Aṅgiras</s>es. Within these are the three <s>Vedas</s>; <s>Bhṛgu</s>s follow the <s>Aṅgiras</s>es. The flower of the waters, form, space — [this is] the supreme purifier.' Having sipped and sprinkled, he consecrates himself [with the mantra]: '<s>Indra</s>, live!' Thus [says] the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. (GpBr 1,1.39)

children.text: Gopathabrāhmaṇa, Pūrvabhāga, Dvitīyaḥ prapāṭhakaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Gopatha Brāhmaṇa</s>, Prior Section (<s>Pūrvabhāga</s>), Second Lesson (<s>Dvitīyaḥ prapāṭhakaḥ</s>).

children.text: oṃ brahmacārīṣṇaṃś carati rodasī ubhe ity ācāryam āha / tasmin devāḥ sammanaso bhavantīti vāyum āha sa sadya eti pūrvasmād uttaraṃ samudram ity ādityam āha dīkṣito dīrghaśmaśrur eṣa dīkṣita eṣa dīrghaśmaśrur eṣa evācāryasthāne tiṣṭhann ācārya iti stūyate vaidyutasthāne tiṣṭhan vāyur iti stūyate dyausthāne tiṣṭhann āditya iti stūyate / tad apy etad ṛcoktaṃ brahmacārīṣṇann iti brāhmaṇam // GpBr_1,2.1 //
children.translated_text: Oṃ. 'The <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate student) wanders, moving across both worlds (heaven and earth)' — this refers to the teacher (<s>ācārya</s>). 'In him the gods become of one mind' — this refers to <s>Vāyu</s> (wind). 'He goes at once from the former to the northern ocean' — this refers to <s>Āditya</s> (the sun). 'He is the consecrated one, the long-bearded one' — this consecrated one, this long-bearded one: standing in the position of the teacher, he is praised as 'the teacher'; standing in the position of lightning, he is praised as 'Vāyu'; standing in the position of heaven, he is praised as '<s>Āditya</s>.' And this too is stated in the <s>ṛc</s>: 'The <s>brahmacārin</s>, wandering...' Thus [says] the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. (GpBr 1,2.1)

children.text: jāyamāno ha vai brāhmaṇaḥ saptendriyāṇy abhijāyante brahmavarcasaṃ ca yaśaś ca svapnaṃ ca krodhaṃ ca ślāghāṃ ca rūpaṃ ca puṇyam eva gandhaṃ saptamam / tāni ha vā asyaitāni brahmacaryam upetopakrāmanti mṛgān asya brahmavarcasaṃ gacchaty ācāryaṃ yaśo 'jagaraṃ svapno varāhaṃ krodhopaślāghaṃ kumārīṃ rūpam oṣadhivanaspatīn puṇyo gandhaḥ sa yan mṛgājināni vaste tena tad brahmavarcasam avarundhe yad asya mṛgeṣu bhavati saha snāto brahmavarcasī bhavati sa yad aharahar ācāryāya karmakarīti tena tad yaśo 'varundhe yad asyācārye bhavati saha snāto yaśasvī bhavati sa yat suṣupsur nidrānninayati tena taṃ svapnam avarundhe yo 'syājagare bhavati taṃ ha snātasvapantam āhuḥ svapitum ainaṃ bobudhatheti sa kruddho vācā na kaṃcana hinasti puruṣāt puruṣāt pāpīyān iva manyamānas tena taṃ krodham avarundhe yo 'sya varāhe bhavati tasya ha snātasya krodhāślāghīyasaṃ viśante 'thādbhiḥ ślāghyamāno na snāyāt tena taṃ ślāghām avarundhe yāsyāpsu bhavati saha snātaḥ ślāghīyo 'nnebhyaḥ ślāghyo 'thaitad brahmacāriṇo rūpaṃ yat kumāryās tān nagnān nīdīkṣedetiveti mukhaṃ viparidhāpayet tena tad rūpam avarundhe yad asya kumāryāṃ bhavati taṃ ha snātaṃ kumārīm iva nirīkṣante 'thaid brahmacāriṇaḥ puṇyo gandho ya oṣadhivanaspatīnāṃ tāsāṃ puṇyaṃ gandhaṃ pracchidya nopajighret tena taṃ puṇyaṃ gandham avarundhe yo 'syauṣadhivanaspatīṣu bhavati sa ha snātaḥ puṇyagandhir bhavati // GpBr_1,2.2 //
children.translated_text: When a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is born, seven faculties are born with him: <s>brahmavarcas</s> (sacred splendor), fame (<s>yaśas</s>), sleep (<s>svapna</s>), anger (<s>krodha</s>), self-praise (<s>ślāghā</s>), beauty (<s>rūpa</s>), and a holy fragrance as the seventh. These [faculties] of his depart when he enters upon <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate studentship): his <s>brahmavarcas</s> goes to the deer, his fame to the teacher, his sleep to the python (<s>ajagara</s>), his anger to the boar, his self-praise to the maiden (<s>kumārī</s>), his beauty to the herbs and trees, [and] his holy fragrance [also to the herbs and trees]. Because he wears deerskins, thereby he recovers that <s>brahmavarcas</s> which was in the deer; having completed [his studentship], having bathed [as a <s>snātaka</s>], he becomes possessed of <s>brahmavarcas</s>. Because he performs service for the teacher day after day, thereby he recovers that fame which was in the teacher; having bathed, he becomes famous. Because, desiring to sleep, he drives away drowsiness, thereby he recovers that sleep which was in the python; of that bathed [<s>snātaka</s>] who sleeps, they say: 'Wake him, let him sleep [properly].' Because when angry he harms no one with speech, considering himself worse than any person, thereby he recovers that anger which was in the boar; of that bathed [<s>snātaka</s>], those desiring anger and self-praise approach [him]. Moreover, while being praised, one should not bathe [i.e., should not end studentship prematurely]; thereby he recovers that self-praise which was in the waters; having bathed, he becomes more praiseworthy than all for food, praiseworthy. And this is the beauty of a <s>brahmacārin</s> which [came from] the maiden: he should not look at them naked — 'Avert [your face]!' — he should turn his face away; thereby he recovers that beauty which was in the maiden; that bathed [<s>snātaka</s>] — maidens gaze upon him as upon a maiden. And this is the holy fragrance of the <s>brahmacārin</s> which [came from] the herbs and trees: having plucked their holy fragrance, he should not smell it; thereby he recovers that holy fragrance which was in the herbs and trees; having bathed, he becomes one of holy fragrance. (GpBr 1.2.2)

children.text: sa vā eṣa upayaṃś caturdhopaity agniṃ pādenācāryaṃ pādena grāmaṃ pādena mṛtyuṃ pādena sa yad aharahaḥ samidha āhṛtya sāyaṃ prātar agniṃ paricaret tena taṃ pādam avarundhe yo 'syāgnau bhavati / sa yad aharahar ācāryāya karma karoti tena taṃ pādam avarundhe yo 'sya ācārye bhavati / sa yad aharahar grāmaṃ praviśya bhikṣām eva parīpsati na maithunaṃ tena taṃ pādam avarundhe yo 'sya grāme bhavati sa yat kruddho vācā na kaṃcana hinasti puruṣāt puruṣāt pāpīyāni manyamānas tenaiva taṃ pādam avarundhe yo 'sya mṛtyau bhavati // GpBr_1,2.3 //
children.translated_text: This student (<s>upayaṃ</s>), approaching, enters into four [entities] with a quarter each: into <s>Agni</s> (fire) with a quarter, into the teacher with a quarter, into the village with a quarter, and into death with a quarter. Because day after day he brings fuel-sticks and tends the fire morning and evening, thereby he recovers that quarter of his which was in <s>Agni</s>. Because day after day he performs service for the teacher, thereby he recovers that quarter of his which was in the teacher. Because day after day, entering the village, he seeks only alms and not sexual union, thereby he recovers that quarter of his which was in the village. Because when angry he harms no one with speech, considering himself worse than any person, thereby he recovers that very quarter of his which was in death. (GpBr 1.2.3)

children.text: pañca ha vā ete brahmacāriṇy agnayo dhīyante dvau pṛthagghastayor mukhe hṛdaya upastha eva pañcamaḥ / sa yad dakṣiṇena pāṇinā striyaṃ na spṛśati tenāharahar yājināṃ lokam avarundhe yat savyena tena pravrājināṃ yan mukhena tenāgnipraskandināṃ yaddhṛdayena tena śūrāṇāṃ yad upasthena tena gṛhamedhināṃ taiś cet striyaṃ parāharaty anagnir iva śiṣyate / sa yad aharahar ācāryāya kule 'nutiṣṭhate so 'nuṣṭhāya brūyād dharmagupto mā gopāyeti dharmo hainaṃ gupto gopāyeti tasya ha prajā śvaḥ śvaḥ śreyasī śreyasī ha bhavati dhāyyaiva pratidhīyate svarge loke pitṝn nidadhāti tāntavaṃ na vasīta yas tāntavaṃ vaste kṣatraṃ vardhate na brahma tasmāt tāntavaṃ na vasīta brahma vardhatāṃ mā kṣatram iti nopary āsīta yad upary āste prāṇam eva tadātmane 'dharaṃ kurute yad vāto vahati adha evāsīta adhaḥ śayīta adhas tiṣṭhed adho vrajed evaṃ ha sma vaitat pūrve brāhmaṇā brahmacaryaṃ caranti taṃ ha sma tatputraṃ bhrātaraṃ vopatāpinam āhur upanayetainam ity āsamiddhārāt svareṣyanto 'nnam adyād athāha jaghanam āhuḥ snāpayetainam ity āsamiddhārān na hy etāni vratāni bhavanti taṃ cecchayānam ācāryo 'bhivadet sa pratisaṃhāya pratiśṛṇuyāt taṃ cecchayānam upytāya taṃ ced utthitam abhiprakramya taṃ ced abhiprakrāntam abhipalāyamānam evaṃ ha sma vaitat pūrve brāhmaṇā brahmacaryaṃ caranti teṣāṃ ha sma vaiṣā puṇyā kīrtir gacchaty āha vā ayaṃ so 'dya gamiṣyatīti // GpBr_1,2.4 //
children.translated_text: Indeed, five fires are placed in the <s>brahmacārin</s> (Vedic student) — two separately in his hands, [one] in his mouth, [one in his] heart, and the fifth in his generative organ. When he does not touch a woman with his right hand, by that he day after day wins the world of those who sacrifice (<s>yājins</s>); when [he does not touch her] with his left hand, by that [he wins the world] of the wandering ascetics (<s>pravrājins</s>); when [he does not touch her] with his mouth, by that [he wins the world] of those who leap into the fire (<s>agnipraskandins</s>); when [he does not touch her] with his heart, by that [he wins the world] of the heroes (<s>śūras</s>); when [he does not touch her] with his generative organ, by that [he wins the world] of the householders (<s>gṛhamedins</s>). But if he carries off a woman with these [five fires], he is left as though without fire. When he day after day serves the teacher (<s>ācārya</s>) in the household, having served, he should say: 'Protected by <s>Dharma</s> (righteousness), protect me!' <s>Dharma</s>, being protected, indeed protects him. His progeny becomes better and better, day after day; he is established just as [the fire] is established in the fire-holder; he places his forefathers in the heavenly world. He should not wear woven [cloth]; whoever wears woven [cloth], the <s>Kṣatra</s> (ruling power) increases, not <s>Brahman</s> (priestly power); therefore he should not wear woven [cloth] — 'Let <s>Brahman</s> increase, not <s>Kṣatra</s>!' He should not sit on an elevated [seat]; when he sits on high, he makes the breath (<s>prāṇa</s>) lower for himself — that which the wind carries [away]. He should sit low, he should lie low, he should stand low, he should walk low. Thus indeed did the ancient <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s practice <s>brahmacarya</s> (the vow of Vedic studentship). They would say of such a one — a son, a brother, or a tormented one — 'Let him be initiated (<s>upanīta</s>)!' From the fire-kindling onward, while intending to recite the <s>Svara</s>s (accented formulas), he may eat food. But then, as to the latter part, they say: 'Let him be bathed (graduated)!' — from the fire-kindling onward, for these observances do not [then any longer] exist. If the teacher (<s>ācārya</s>) should address him while he is lying down, he should gather himself up and respond. If [the teacher approaches] him while lying down, [he should] rise up; if [the teacher approaches] him while standing, [he should] walk toward [him]; if [the teacher approaches] him while already walking, [he should follow] running after [him]. Thus indeed did the ancient <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s practice <s>brahmacarya</s>. Their meritorious fame would spread — [people] would say: 'Indeed, this one will go [to the heavenly world] today.'

children.text: janamejayo ha vai pārīkṣito mṛgayāṃ cariṣyan haṃsābhyām aśikṣann upāvatastha iti tāv ūcatur janamejayaṃ pārīkṣitam abhyājagāma sa hovāca namo vāṃ bhagavantau kau nu bhagavantāv iti tāv ūcatur dakṣiṇāgniś cāhavanīyaś ceti sa hovāca namo vāṃ bhagavantau tadākīyatām iti hopārāmam ity api kila devā na ramante na hi devā na ramante 'pi caikopārāmād devā ārāmam upasaṃkrāmantīti sa hovāca namo vāṃ bhagavantau kiṃ puṇyam iti brahmacaryam iti kiṃ laukyam iti brahmacaryam eveti tat ko veda iti dantāvalo dhaumro 'tha khalu dantāvalo dhaumro yāvati tāvati kāle pārīkṣitaṃ janamejayam abhyājagāma tasmā uptyāya svayam eva viṣṭaraṃ nidadhau tam upasaṃgṛhya papracchādhīhi bho kiṃ puṇyam iti brahmacaryam iti kiṃ laukyam iti brahmacaryam eveti tasmā etat provācāṣṭācatvāriṃśad varṣaṃ sarvavedabrahmacaryaṃ tac caturdhā vedeṣu vyūhya dvādaśavarṣaṃ brahmacaryaṃ dvādaśavarṣāṇy avarārdham api stāyaṃś cared yathāśakty aparam / tasmā uhasy ṛṣabhau sahasraṃ dadāv apy apikīrtitam ācāryo brahmacārīty eka āhur ākāśam adhidaivatam athādhyātmaṃ brāhmaṇo vratavāṃś caraṇavān brahmacārī // GpBr_1,2.5 //
children.translated_text: <s>Janamejaya</s>, the son of <s>Parīkṣit</s>, while about to go hunting, came upon two swans and stood near them learning [from them]. They spoke to <s>Janamejaya</s>, the son of <s>Parīkṣit</s>, who approached and said: 'Salutations to you, venerable ones! Who are you, venerable ones?' They replied: 'The <s>Dakṣiṇāgni</s> (southern fire) and the <s>Āhavanīya</s> (offering fire).' He said: 'Salutations to you, venerable ones! Then let it be taught.' 'Stop!' [they said]. 'But even the gods do not stop; indeed the gods do not stop. Yet from stopping at one [point], the gods proceed to the [next] place of rest.' He said: 'Salutations to you, venerable ones! What is meritorious?' '<s>Brahmacarya</s> (Vedic studentship).' 'What is worldly [merit]?' '<s>Brahmacarya</s> alone.' 'Who knows that?' '<s>Dantāvala Dhaumra</s>.' Then indeed <s>Dantāvala Dhaumra</s>, after some time, approached <s>Janamejaya</s>, the son of <s>Parīkṣit</s>. For him [<s>Janamejaya</s>] rose and himself placed a seat. Having embraced him, he asked: 'Teach, sir! What is meritorious?' '<s>Brahmacarya</s>.' 'What is worldly [merit]?' '<s>Brahmacarya</s> alone.' He then declared to him: 'Forty-eight years is the <s>brahmacarya</s> (Vedic studentship) for all the <s>Veda</s>s; that, divided fourfold among the <s>Veda</s>s, is twelve years of <s>brahmacarya</s> [per Veda]. For twelve years one should practice the latter half [at minimum], or as long as one is able, the remainder.' He gave him two bulls and a thousand [cows], and [thus] he was celebrated. 'The teacher and the student are one,' say some. Space (<s>ākāśa</s>) is the presiding deity; and with regard to the self (<s>adhyātma</s>), the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who keeps his vows and follows good conduct is the [true] <s>brahmacārin</s>.

children.text: brahma ha vai prajā mṛtyave samprayacchat brahmacāriṇam eva na sampradadau sa hovācāsyām asminn iti kim iti yāṃ rātrīṃ samidham anāhṛtya vaset tām āyuṣo 'varundhīyeti tasmād brahmacāry aharahaḥ samidha āhṛtya sāyaṃ prātar agniṃ paricaret nopary upasādayet atha pratiṣṭhāpayet yad upary upasādayej jīmūtavarṣī tad ahaḥ parjanyo bhavati te devā abruvan brāhmaṇo vā ayaṃ brahmacaryaṃ cariṣyati brūtāsmai bhikṣā iti gṛhapatir brūta bahucārī gṛhapatnyā iti kim asyā vṛñjotādadatyā iti iṣṭāpūrtasukṛtadraviṇam avarundhyād iti tasmād brahmacāriṇe 'harahar bhikṣāṃ dadyād gṛhiṇīm āmeyur iṣṭāpūrtasukṛtadraviṇam avarundhyād iti / saptamīṃ nātinayet saptamīm atinayan na brahmacārī bhavati samidbhaikṣe saptarātram acaritavān brahmacārī punar upaneyo bhavati // GpBr_1,2.6 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> indeed handed over [all] creatures to Death, but the <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate student) alone he did not hand over. He [Death] said: 'Let [something] be for me in this one.' 'What?' 'Whichever night he dwells without having brought fuel — that [night] of his lifespan I would seize.' Therefore the <s>brahmacārin</s> should bring fuel day after day and tend the fire morning and evening. He should not place [the fuel] on top [of the fire]; rather he should establish [the fire properly]. If he were to place [fuel] on top, <s>Parjanya</s> (the Rain-god) would become a thunder-cloud rainer on that day. The gods said: 'This <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> will observe <s>brahmacarya</s>; provide him with alms.' 'Householder, tell [your wife]' — 'He is one who wanders much' — '[tell] the housewife.' 'What would she lose by giving to him?' 'She would seize the merit of sacrifice, charitable works, and good deeds as her wealth.' Therefore one should give alms to the <s>brahmacārin</s> day after day — [the housewife should give], for [in doing so] she would seize the merit of sacrifice, charitable works, and good deeds as her wealth. He should not let the seventh [day] pass [without fuel and alms]. If the seventh passes, he ceases to be a <s>brahmacārin</s>. [If] the <s>brahmacārin</s> has not performed the fuel-and-alms [observance] for seven nights, he must be initiated again.

children.text: nopari śāyī syān na gāyano na nartano na saraṇo na niṣṭhīvet yad upari śāyī bhavaty abhīkṣṇaṃ nivāsā jāyante yad gāyano bhavaty abhīkṣṇaśa ākrandān dhāvante yan nartano bhavaty abhīkṣṇaśaḥ pretān nirharante yat saraṇo bhavaty abhīkṣṇaśaḥ prajāḥ saṃviśante yan niṣṭhīvati madhya eva tadātmano niṣṭhīvati sa cen niṣṭhīved divo nu māṃ yad atrāpi madhor ahaṃ yad atrāpi rasasya ma ity ātmānam anumantrayate / yad atrāpi madhor ahaṃ niriṣṭaviṣamasmṛtaṃ / agniś ca tat savitā ca punar me jaṭhare dhattām / yad atrāpi rasasya me parāpapātāsma tam / tad ihopahvayāmahe tan ma āpyāyatāṃ punar iti / na śmaśānam ātiṣṭhet sa ced abhitiṣṭhed udakaṃ haste kṛtvā yadīdam ṛtukāmyety abhimantrya japaṃt samprokṣya parikrāmet samayāyopari vrajet yadīdam ṛtukāmyāghaṃ ripram upeyima andhaḥ śloṇa iva hīyatām / mā no 'nvāgād aghaṃ yata iti / atha haitad devānāṃ pariṣūtaṃ yad brahmacārī / tad apy etad ṛcoktam / devānām etat pariṣūtam anabhyārūḍhaṃ carati rocamānaṃ tasmin sarve paśavas tatra yajñās tasminn annaṃ saha devatābhir iti brāhmaṇam // GpBr_1,2.7 //
children.translated_text: He should not sleep on a raised [bed]; he should not sing; he should not dance; he should not run; he should not spit. If he sleeps on a raised [bed], frequent deaths occur [in the village]. If he sings, frequent [funeral] wailings run [through the village]. If he dances, frequently corpses are carried out. If he runs, frequently [enemy] people enter [the village]. If he spits, he spits into the very middle of his own self. If he should spit, he should address himself [with this mantra]: 'That of mine which is of honey, and that of mine which is of sap' — [and recite:] 'Whatever of honey in me was spat out and forgotten — may <s>Agni</s> and <s>Savitṛ</s> place that again in my belly. Whatever of my sap has fallen away — that we call back here; may it nourish me again.' He should not stand upon a cremation ground. If he should step upon it, having placed water in his hand, muttering and sprinkling [with the mantra] 'Whatever evil, harm we may have approached here by seasonal desire — may it fall away like a blind, lame [creature]; may evil not follow us from where [we were],' he should circumambulate and pass above [the cremation ground] toward agreement. And indeed, the <s>brahmacārin</s> is the creation of the gods. As this is stated by the <s>Ṛc</s>: 'This is the creation of the gods; it moves shining, unapproached. In it are all cattle; in it the sacrifices; in it is food together with the deities' — thus [says] the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.

children.text: prāṇāpānau janayann iti śaṅkhasya mūle mahaṛṣer vasiṣṭhasya putraḥ etāṃ vācaṃ sasṛje śītoṣṇāv ihotsau prādurbhaveyātām iti tathā tac chaśvad anuvartate atha khalu vipāṇmadhye vasiṣṭhaśilā nāma prathama āśramo dvitīyaḥ kṛṣṇaśilās tasmin vasiṣṭhaḥ samatapad viśvāmitrajamadagnī jāmadagne tapataḥ gautamabharadvājau siṃhau prabhave tapataḥ guṅgur gugur vāse tapaty ṛṣir ṛṣidroṇe 'bhyatapad agastyo 'gastyatīrthe tapati divy atrir ha tapati svayambhūḥ kaśyapaḥ kaśyapatuṅge 'bhyatapad ulavṛkarkṣutarakṣuḥ śvā varāhacilvaṭibabhrukāḥ sarpadaṃṣṭranaḥ saṃhanukṛṇvānāḥ kaśyapatuṅgadarśanāt saraṇavāṭāt siddhir bhavati brāhmyaṃ varṣasahasram ṛṣivane brahmacāry ekapādenātiṣṭhad dvitīyaṃ varṣasahasraṃ mūrdhany evāmṛtasya dhārām adhārayad brāhmāṇy aṣṭācatvāriṃśataṃ varṣasahasrāṇi salilasya pṛṣṭhe śivo 'bhyatapat tasmāt taptāt tapaso bhūya evābhyatapat / tad apyetā ṛco 'bhivadanti prāṇāpānau janayann iti brāhmaṇam // GpBr_1,2.8 //
children.translated_text: 'Generating the in-breath and out-breath' — at the mouth of the conch [shell], the son of the great sage <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>. He created this speech [saying:] 'May cold and heat come forth here.' So it perpetually continues. Now, in the middle of the [river] <s>Vipāś</s> (Beas), there is [a place] called <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>-rock — the first hermitage; the second is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-rock. There <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> performed austerities. <s>Viśvāmitra</s> and <s>Jamadagni</s>, descendants of <s>Jamadagni</s>, perform austerities. <s>Gautama</s> and <s>Bharadvāja</s>, two lions, perform austerities at [the place of] origin. <s>Guṅgu</s> and <s>Gugu</s> perform austerities at the dwelling. The sage performed austerities at <s>Ṛṣidroṇa</s>. <s>Agastya</s> performs austerities at <s>Agastyatīrtha</s>. <s>Atri</s> performs austerities in heaven. The self-born <s>Kaśyapa</s> performed austerities at <s>Kaśyapatuṅga</s> (Kaśyapa's Peak). <s>Ulavṛk</s>, <s>Arkṣuta</s>, <s>Rakṣu</s>, <s>Śvan</s>, <s>Varāha</s>, <s>Cilvaṭi</s>, <s>Babhruka</s>, <s>Sarpadaṃṣṭra</s>, <s>Saṃhanu</s> — the makers. From the sight of <s>Kaśyapatuṅga</s>, from the path of approach, <s>siddhi</s> (perfection) arises. For a thousand divine years the <s>brahmacārin</s> stood on one foot in the forest of the sages. For a second thousand years, he held the stream of nectar on his head. <s>Brahmā</s> performed austerities for forty-eight thousand years on the surface of the waters. <s>Śiva</s> performed austerities. From that heated [one], he performed yet further austerities from austerity. The <s>Ṛc</s> verses also declare this: 'Generating the in-breath and out-breath' — thus [says] the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.

children.text:
ekapād dvipada iti vāyur ekapāt tasyākāśaṃ pādaś candramā dvipāt tasya pūrvapakṣāparapakṣau pādāv ādityas tripāt tasyeme lokāḥ pādā agniḥ ṣaṭpādas tasya pṛthivyantarikṣaṃ dyaur āpa oṣadhivanaspataya imāni bhūtāni pādās teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ vedā gatir ātmā pratiṣṭhitāś catasro brahmaṇaḥ śākhā atho āhuḥ ṣaḍ iti mūrtir ākāśaś cety ṛcā mūrtir yājuṣī gatiḥ sāmamayaṃ tejo bhṛgvaṅgirasām āpaitad brahmaiva yajñaś catuṣpād dviḥ saṃsthita iti / tasya bhṛgvaṅgirasaḥ saṃsthe atho āhur ekasaṃsthita iti yaddhotarcāṃ maṇḍalaiḥ karoti pṛthivīṃ te nāpyāyayati etasyāṃ hy agniś carati / tad apy etad ṛcoktam / agnivāsāḥ pṛthivy asi tanyūr iti / yad adhvaryur yajuṣā karoty antarikṣaṃ tenāpyāyayati tasmin vāyur na niviśate katamac ca nāha iti / tad apy etad ṛcoktam / antarikṣe pathibhir hrīyamāṇo na niviśate katamac ca nāhaḥ / apāṃ yoniḥ prathamajā ṛtasya kva svijjātaḥ kuta ābabhūveti / yad udgātā sāmnā karoti divaṃ tenāpyāyayati tatra hy ādityaḥ śukraś carati / tad apy etad ṛcoktam / uccāyataṃ tam aruṇaṃ suparṇam iti / yad brahmarcāṃ kāṇḍaiḥ karoty apas tenāpyāyayati candramā hy apsu carati / tad apy etad ṛcoktam / candramā apsantar iti / tāsām oṣadhivanaspatayaḥ kāṇḍāni tato mūlakāṇḍaparṇapuṣpaphalapraroharasagandhair yajño vartate 'dbhiḥ karmāṇi pravartante 'dbhiḥ somo viṣūyate tad yad brahmāṇaṃ karmaṇi karmaṇy āmantrayaty apas tenānujānāty eṣo hy asya bhāgas tad yathā bhokṣyamāṇo 'pa eva prathamam ācāmayed apa upariṣṭād evaṃ yajño 'dbhir eva pravartate 'psu saṃsthāpyate tasmād brahmā purastāddhomasaṃsthitahomair yajño vartate 'ntarā hi purastāddhomasaṃsthitahomair yajña parigṛhṇāty antarā hi bhṛgvaṅgirasaḥ vedānoduhya bhṛgvaṅgirasaḥ somapānaṃ manyante somātmako hy ayaṃ veda / tad apy etad ṛcoktam / somaṃ manyate papivān
iti / tad yathemāṃ pṛthivīm udīrṇāṃ jyotiṣā dhūmāyamānāṃ varṣaṃ śamayaty evam brahmā bhṛgvaṅgirobhir vyāhṛtibhir yajñasya viriṣṭaṃ śamayaty agnir ādityāya ma ity ete 'ṅgirasa eta idaṃ sarvaṃ samāpnuvanti vāyur āpaś candramā ity ete bhṛgava eta idaṃ sarvaṃ samāpyāyayanty ekam eva saṃsthaṃ bhavatīti brāhmaṇam // GpBr_1,2.9 //
children.translated_text: 'One-footed, two-footed' — <s>Vāyu</s> (wind) is one-footed; space (<s>ākāśa</s>) is his foot. <s>Candramās</s> (the moon) is two-footed; the bright and dark fortnights are his feet. <s>Āditya</s> (the sun) is three-footed; these worlds are his feet. <s>Agni</s> (fire) is six-footed; the earth, atmosphere, heaven, waters, herbs and trees, and these beings are his feet. Of all these, the <s>Vedas</s> are the course, the self, the foundation. There are four branches of <s>Brahman</s>; though they say six — the embodied form and space. The <s>Ṛc</s> (verse) is the form; the <s>Yajus</s> (sacrificial formula) is the movement; the <s>Sāman</s> (chant) is the radiance; of the <s>Bhṛgvaṅgirasas</s>, the waters — this is indeed <s>Brahman</s>. The sacrifice (<s>yajña</s>) is four-footed, established in two [foundations]. The <s>Bhṛgvaṅgirasas</s> are its two foundations. Though they say 'established in one' — when the <s>Hotṛ</s> (invoking priest) performs with <s>Ṛc</s> verses arranged in <s>maṇḍalas</s> (books), he thereby nourishes the earth, for <s>Agni</s> moves upon it. As the <s>Ṛc</s> verse also states: 'O Earth, you are clad in fire, the warp.' When the <s>Adhvaryu</s> (officiating priest) performs with the <s>Yajus</s>, he thereby nourishes the atmosphere; in it <s>Vāyu</s> moves without settling, and never ceases. As the <s>Ṛc</s> also states: 'Carried along the paths in the atmosphere, he never settles, never ceases; the womb of waters, the firstborn of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order) — where indeed was he born, whence did he arise?' When the <s>Udgātṛ</s> (chanting priest) performs with the <s>Sāman</s>, he thereby nourishes the heaven, for the bright <s>Āditya</s> moves there. As the <s>Ṛc</s> also states: 'That lofty, tawny, beautiful-winged one.' When the <s>Brahmán</s> (supervising priest) performs with sections of <s>Ṛc</s> verses, he thereby nourishes the waters, for the moon moves in the waters. As the <s>Ṛc</s> also states: 'The moon within the waters.' Of those [waters], herbs and trees are the sections; from their roots, stalks, leaves, flowers, fruits, sprouts, juices, and fragrances the sacrifice proceeds. Through the waters, the ritual actions proceed; through the waters, <s>Soma</s> is distributed. When the <s>Brahmán</s> priest is consulted in each ritual act, he thereby authorizes the waters, for that is his share. Just as one about to eat first sips water, and water is [taken] at the end — so the sacrifice proceeds through the waters and is concluded in the waters. Therefore the <s>Brahmán</s> [directs] the sacrifice through preliminary and concluding oblations, for he encompasses the sacrifice through the preliminary and concluding oblations. For the <s>Bhṛgvaṅgirasas</s>, having milked the <s>Vedas</s>, consider it <s>Soma</s>-drinking, for this <s>Veda</s> is of the nature of <s>Soma</s>. As the <s>Ṛc</s> also states: 'He thinks he has drunk <s>Soma</s>.' Just as rain pacifies this earth when it has been inflamed and smoking with fire, so the <s>Brahmán</s> priest pacifies the deficiency of the sacrifice with the <s>Bhṛgvaṅgiras</s> <s>vyāhṛtis</s>. '<s>Agni</s>, <s>Āditya</s>, Ma' — these are the <s>Aṅgirasas</s>; they encompass all this. '<s>Vāyu</s>, the waters, <s>Candramās</s>' — these are the <s>Bhṛgus</s>; they nourish all this. It becomes one single foundation — thus [says] the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. // GpBr 1,2.9 //

children.text: vicārī ha vai kāvandhiḥ kabandhasyātharvaṇasya putro medhāvī mīmāṃsako 'nūcāna āsa sa ha svenātimānena mānuṣaṃ vittaṃ neyāya taṃ mātovāca ta evaitad annam avocaṃs ta imam eṣu kurupañcāleṣv aṅgamagadheṣu kāśikausalyeṣu śālvamatsyeṣu śavasauśīnareṣūdīcyeṣv annam adantīty atha vayaṃ tavaivātimāne nānādyāsmo vatsa vāhanam anviccheti sa māndhātur yauvanāśvasya sārvabhaumasya rājñaḥ somaṃ prasūtam ājagāma sa sado 'nupraviśyartvijaś ca yajamānaṃ cāmantrayāmāsa tad yāḥ prācyo nadyo vahanti yāś ca dakṣiṇācyo yāś ca pratīcyo yāś ca udīcyas tāḥ sarvāḥ pṛthaṅ nāma dheyor ity ācakṣate tāsāṃ samudram abhipadyamānānāṃ chidyate nāmadheyaṃ samudra ity ācakṣate evam ime sarve vedā nirmitāḥ sakalpāḥ sarahasyāḥ sabrāhmaṇāḥ sopaniṣatkāḥ setihāsāḥ sānvākhyātāḥ sapurāṇāḥ sasvarāḥ sasaṃskārāḥ saniruktāḥ sānuśāsanāḥ sānumārjanāḥ savākovākyās teṣāṃ yajñam abhipadyamānānāṃ chidyate nāmadheyaṃ yajña ity evācakṣate // GpBr_1,2.10 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vicārin</s>, son of <s>Kabandha Ātharvaṇa</s>, of the <s>Kāvandhi</s> lineage, was indeed a learned, inquiring, well-studied [scholar]. Through his own excessive pride, he brought his human wealth to ruin. His mother said to him: 'Those [scholars] have said this [to you as] food — they eat food among these <s>Kuru-Pañcālas</s>, <s>Aṅga-Magadhas</s>, <s>Kāśi-Kausalyas</s>, <s>Śālva-Matsyas</s>, and the <s>Śava-Sauśīnaras</s> of the north. But we, through your excessive pride alone, are without food, dear child. Seek a vehicle [of livelihood]!' He came to the <s>Soma</s> pressing that had been authorized by King <s>Māndhātṛ Yauvanāśva</s>, the universal sovereign. Having entered the assembly hall, he addressed the officiating priests and the sacrificer: 'Those rivers that flow eastward, those that flow southward, those westward, and those northward — all of them are called by their individual names. But when they reach the ocean, their individual names are cut off; they are called simply "ocean." In the same way, all these <s>Vedas</s> — with their <s>kalpas</s> (ritual manuals), with their esoteric teachings (<s>rahasya</s>), with their <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, with their <s>Upaniṣads</s>, with their <s>Itihāsas</s> (epics), with their <s>Anvākhyānas</s> (narratives), with their <s>Purāṇas</s> (ancient lore), with their accents (<s>svara</s>), with their ritual refinements (<s>saṃskāra</s>), with their etymologies (<s>nirukta</s>), with their instructions (<s>anuśāsana</s>), with their purifications (<s>anumārjana</s>), with their dialogues (<s>vākovākya</s>) — when they reach the sacrifice, their individual names are cut off; they are called simply "the sacrifice (<s>yajña</s>)."' // GpBr 1,2.10 //

children.text: bhūmir ha vai etad vicchinnaṃ devayajanaṃ yad aprāk pravaṇaṃ yad anudak pravaṇaṃ yat kṛtrimaṃ yat samaviṣamam idaṃ ha tv eva devayajanaṃ yat samaṃ samūlam avidagdhaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ prāg udak pravaṇaṃ samaṃ samāstīrṇam iva bhavati yatra brāhmaṇasya brāhmaṇatāṃ vidyād brahmā brahmatvaṃ karotīti voce chandas tan na vindāmo yenottaram emahīti / tān ha papraccha kiṃ vidvān hotā hautraṃ karoti kiṃ vidvān adhvaryur ādhvaryavaṃ karoti kiṃ vidvān udgātaudgātraṃ karoti kiṃ vidvān brahmā brahmatvaṃ karotīti voce chandas tan na vindāmo yenottaram emahīti / te brūmo vāg eva hotā hautraṃ karoti vāco hi stomāś ca vaṣaṭkārāś cābhisaṃpadyante te brūmo vāg eva hotā vāg brahma vāk deva iti / prāṇāpānābhyām evādhvaryur ādhvaryavaṃ karoti prāṇaḥ praṇītāni ha bhūtāni prāṇaḥ praṇītā praṇītās te brūmaḥ prāṇāpānāv evādhvaryū prāṇāpānau brahma prāṇāpānau deva iti / cakṣuṣaivodgātā audgātraṃ karoti cakṣuṣā hīmāni bhūtāni paśyanty atho cakṣur evodgātā cakṣur brahma cakṣur deva iti / manasaiva brahmā brahmatvaṃ karoti manasā hi tiryak ca diśa ūrdhvaṃ ca yac ca kiṃca manasaiva karoti tad brahma te brūmo mana eva brahmā mano brahma mano deva iti // GpBr_1,2.11 //
children.translated_text: The earth is indeed a defective sacrificial ground (<s>devayajana</s>) when it does not slope eastward, when it does not slope northward, when it is artificial, or when it is uneven. But this indeed is [a proper] sacrificial ground: that which is level, with natural soil, unscorched, firm, sloping toward the east and north, level, and appears as if spread evenly. Where one would recognize the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>-hood of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> — 'The <s>brahmán</s> priest fulfills the office of <s>Brahman</s>' — they said: 'We do not find the [sacred] meter (<s>chandas</s>) by which we may go beyond.' He asked them: 'Knowing what does the <s>hotṛ</s> (invoking priest) perform the <s>hautra</s> (invoking)? Knowing what does the <s>adhvaryu</s> (officiating priest) perform the <s>ādhvaryava</s> (officiating)? Knowing what does the <s>udgātṛ</s> (chanting priest) perform the <s>audgātra</s> (chanting)? Knowing what does the <s>brahmán</s> (supervising priest) perform the office of <s>Brahman</s>?' They said: 'We do not find the meter by which we may go beyond.' 'We declare: Speech (<s>Vāc</s>) alone is the <s>hotṛ</s> who performs the <s>hautra</s>; for the hymns of praise (<s>stoma</s>) and the <s>vaṣaṭ</s>-calls arise from Speech. We declare: Speech alone is the <s>hotṛ</s>; Speech is <s>Brahman</s>; Speech is the deity.' 'By the in-breath and out-breath (<s>prāṇāpāna</s>) alone does the <s>adhvaryu</s> perform the <s>ādhvaryava</s>; for the beings are led forth by <s>prāṇa</s>; <s>prāṇa</s> is the leader; they are the led forth. We declare: the in-breath and out-breath are indeed the <s>adhvaryus</s>; they are <s>Brahman</s>; they are the deity.' 'By sight (<s>cakṣus</s>) alone does the <s>udgātṛ</s> perform the <s>audgātra</s>; for by sight do these beings see. Thus, sight is indeed the <s>udgātṛ</s>; sight is <s>Brahman</s>; sight is the deity.' 'By the mind (<s>manas</s>) alone does the <s>brahmán</s> perform the office of <s>Brahman</s>; for by the mind [one acts] in the transverse directions and upward, and whatever else — by the mind alone one does it; that is <s>Brahman</s>. We declare: the mind alone is the <s>brahmán</s>; the mind is <s>Brahman</s>; the mind is the deity.' (GpBr 1.2.11)

children.text: tad yathā ha vā idaṃ yajamānaś ca yājayitāraś ca divaṃ brūyuḥ pṛthivīti pṛthivīṃ vāk dyaur iti brūyus tad anyo nānujānāty etām evaṃ nānujānāti yad etad brūyād atha nu katham iti hotety eva hotāraṃ brūyād vāg iti vācaṃ brahmeti brahma deva iti devam adhvaryur ity evādhvaryuṃ brūyāt prāṇāpānāv iti prāṇāpānau brahmeti brahma deva iti devam udgātety evodgātāraṃ brūyāc cakṣur iti cakṣur brahmeti brahma deva iti devaṃ brahmety eva brahmāṇaṃ brūyān mana iti mano brahmeti brahma deva iti devam // GpBr_1,2.12 //
children.translated_text: Just as the sacrificer and the officiating priests might call heaven 'earth' and earth 'heaven' — another would not approve that; one does not approve [such speech]. If someone were to say 'But then how?' — one should call the <s>hotṛ</s> simply '<s>hotṛ</s>' [and identify it with] Speech, <s>Brahman</s>, the deity; one should call the <s>adhvaryu</s> simply '<s>adhvaryu</s>' [and identify it with] the in-breath and out-breath, <s>Brahman</s>, the deity; one should call the <s>udgātṛ</s> simply '<s>udgātṛ</s>' [and identify it with] sight, <s>Brahman</s>, the deity; one should call the <s>brahmán</s> simply '<s>brahmán</s>' [and identify it with] the mind, <s>Brahman</s>, the deity. (GpBr 1.2.12)

children.text: nānā pravacanāni ha vā etāni bhūtāni bhavanti ye caivāsomapaṃ yājayanti ye ca surāpaṃ ye ca brāhmaṇaṃ vicchinnaṃ somayājinaṃ taṃ prātaḥ samitpāṇaya upodeyur upāyāmo bhavantam iti kim artham iti yān eva no bhavāṃs tāṃ hy apraśnān apṛcchad yān eva no bhavān vyācakṣīyeti tatheti tebhya etān praśnān vyācacaṣṭe tad yena ha vā idaṃ vidyamānaṃ cāvidyamānaṃ cābhinidadhāti tad brahma tad yo veda sa brāhmaṇo 'dhīyāno 'dhītyācakṣata iti brāhmaṇam // GpBr_1,2.13 //
children.translated_text: Various indeed are these teachings of beings. Those who have [a non-<s>Soma</s>-drinker] perform a sacrifice, and those who [have] a liquor-drinker [perform], and those who [have] a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who is cut off [from proper practice] — that <s>Soma</s>-sacrificer — they should approach him in the morning with fuel-sticks [in hand, saying]: 'We approach you, sir.' 'For what purpose?' 'Those very questions which you, sir, [asked us] — those unanswered questions — please explain them to us, sir.' 'So be it.' He explained these questions to them. That by which one establishes both the existent and the non-existent — that is <s>Brahman</s>. He who knows this is a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. Having studied, having studied, he declared — thus [says] the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. (GpBr 1.2.13)

children.text: athāto devayajanāny ātmā devayajanaṃ śraddhā devayajanam ṛtvijo devayajanaṃ bhaumaṃ devayajanaṃ tad vā etad ātmā devayajanaṃ yad upavyāyacchamāno vānupavyāyacchamāno vā śarīram adhivasaty eṣa yajña eṣa yajata etaṃ yajanta etad devayajanam athaitat śraddhā devayajanaṃ yadaiva kadācid ādadyāt śraddhā tv evainaṃ nātīyāt tad devayajanam athaitad ṛtvijo devayajanaṃ yatra kvacid brāhmaṇo vidyāvān mantreṇa karoti tad devayajanam athaitad bhaumaṃ devayajanaṃ yatrāpas tiṣṭhanti yatra syandanti pra tad vahanty udvahanti tad devayajanaṃ yat samaṃ samūlam avidagdhaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ prāg udak pravaṇaṃ samaṃ samāstīrṇam iva bhavati yasya śvabhrakūrmo vṛkṣaḥ parvato nadī panthā vā purastāt syān na devayajanamātraṃ purastāt paryavaśiṣyen nottarato 'gneḥ paryupasīderann iti brāhmaṇam // GpBr_1,2.14 //
children.translated_text: Now, then, the sacrificial grounds (<s>devayajana</s>): the self (<s>ātman</s>) is a sacrificial ground; faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) is a sacrificial ground; the priests (<s>ṛtvij</s>) are a sacrificial ground; the earthly [place] is a sacrificial ground. The self is indeed the sacrificial ground in that, whether making effort or not making effort, one inhabits the body — this is the sacrifice, this is the sacrificer, these sacrifice, this is the sacrificial ground. And faith is the sacrificial ground in that, whenever one would take [something for the sacrifice], faith should never abandon him — that is the sacrificial ground. And the priests are the sacrificial ground in that wherever a learned <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> performs [a rite] with a <s>mantra</s> — that is the sacrificial ground. And the earthly [place] is the sacrificial ground: where waters stand, where they flow, [where they] carry forth and carry up — that is the sacrificial ground; that which is level, with natural soil, unscorched, firm, sloping toward the east and north, level, appearing as if spread evenly. [But a place] before which there is a pit, a tortoise[-shaped mound], a tree, a mountain, a river, or a road — not even the measure of a sacrificial ground should remain before [it]; they should not sit to the north of the fire — thus [says] the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. (GpBr 1.2.14)

children.text: aditir vai prajākāmaudanam apacat tata ucchiṣṭam aśnāt so garbham adhatta tata ādityā ajāyanta ya eṣa odanaḥ pacyata ārambhaṇam evaitat kriyate ākramaṇam eva prādeśamātrīḥ samidho bhavanty etāvāṃ hy ātmā prajāpatinā saṃmito 'gner vai yā yajñiyā tanūr aśvatthe tayā samagacchata eṣā svadhṛtyā tanūr yad ghṛtaṃ yad ghṛtena samidho 'nakti tābhyām evainaṃ taṃ tanūbhyāṃ samardhayati yan nirmārgasyādadhāty avakūtyā vai vīryaṃ kriyate yan nirmārgasyādadhāty avakūtyā eva saṃvatsaro vai prajananam agniḥ prajananam etat prajananaṃ yat saṃvatsara ṛcāgnau samidham ādadhāti prajananād evainaṃ tat prajanayitā prajanayaty avaty attur vai puruṣo na hi tad veda yad attum abhijāyate yan nakṣatraṃ tad āpnoti ya eṣa odanaḥ pacyate yonir evaiṣā kriyate yat samidha ādhīyante retas tat dhrīyate saṃvatsaro vai reto hitaṃ prajāyate ye saṃvatsare pary ete 'gnim ādhatte prajāpatir evainam ādhatte dvādaśasu rātrīṣu purā saṃvatsarasyādheyāt tā hi saṃvatsarasya pratimā atho tisṛṣv atho dvayor atho pūrvedyur ādheyāt te vā agnim ādadhānenādityā vā ita uttaram eṣa me 'muṣmiṃl loka āyaṃs te pathi rakṣanta iyan tad u yakṣyamāṇaṃ pratinudanta uccheṣaṇabhājā vā ādityā yad ucchiṣṭaṃ yad ucchiṣṭena samidho 'nakti tebhya eva provāca tebhya eva procya svargaṃ lokaṃ yanti // GpBr_1,2.15 //
children.translated_text: <s>Aditi</s> indeed, desiring offspring, cooked the rice porridge (<s>odana</s>). From the remnant [of that offering], she ate; she conceived a womb [embryo]; from that, the <s>Āditya</s>s were born. This rice porridge that is cooked — that is the beginning; it is the stepping forth. The fuel sticks are a span in length, for the Self is of this measure, as measured by <s>Prajāpati</s>. The sacrificial body of <s>Agni</s> — he united with it in the <s>aśvattha</s> (fig tree). This is the self-sustaining body, which is ghee. When one anoints the fuel sticks with ghee, by those two bodies one strengthens him. When one places [the fuel] outside the path — by concealment indeed power is exercised. When one places it outside the path — by concealment indeed is the year. The year is procreation; <s>Agni</s> is procreation. This is the procreation that is the year. With a <s>ṛc</s> one places fuel on the fire — from procreation itself the procreator procreates. [Yet] the person is eaten by the eater, for he does not know what he was born to eat. What constellation one reaches — this rice porridge that is cooked — it is the womb that is created. When the fuel sticks are placed — that is the seed that is deposited. The year is the deposited seed; it is born [from that]. Those who place the fire at the end of the year — <s>Prajāpati</s> himself places it. [It may be placed] in twelve nights before the year's fire-placement, for those are the images of the year; or in three [nights], or in two, or on the day before the fire-placement. Those <s>Āditya</s>s indeed, for one who places the fire, [provide protection]; 'From here onward, in the other world, may they guard my path' — they indeed drive back [obstacles] for one about to sacrifice. The <s>Āditya</s>s are sharers of the remnant; what is the remnant — when one anoints the fuel sticks with the remnant, one has declared [this] to them; having declared [this] to them, they go to the heavenly world. (GpBr 1,2.15)

children.text: prajāpatir atharvā devaḥ sa tapas taptvaitaṃ cātuṣprāśyaṃ brahmaudanaṃ niramimata caturlokaṃ caturdevaṃ caturvedaṃ catur hautram iti catvāro vā ime lokāḥ pṛthivy antarikṣaṃ dyaur āpa iti catvāro vā ime devā agnir vāyur ādityaś candramāḥ catvāro vā ime vedā ṛgvedo yajurvedaḥ sāmavedo brahmaveda iti catasro vā ime hotrā hautram ādhvaryavam audgātraṃ brahmatvam iti / tad apy etad ṛcoktam / catvāri śṛṅgās trayo 'sya pādā dve śīrṣe sapta hastāso asya / tridhā baddho vṛṣabho roravīti mahodevo martyām āviveśa iti / catvāri śṛṅgeti vedā vā eta uktāḥ trayo 'sya pādā iti savanāny eva dve śīrṣa iti brahmaudanapravargyāv eva sapta hastāso asyeti chandāṃsy eva tridhā baddha iti mantraḥ kalpo brāhmaṇaṃ vṛṣabho roravīty eṣa ha vai vṛṣabha eṣa tad roravīti yad yajñeṣu śastrāṇi śaṃsaty ṛgbhir yajurbhiḥ sāmabhir brahmabhir iti mahodevo martyām āviveśety eṣa ha vai mahān devo yad yajña eṣu martyām āviveśa / yo vidyāt sapta pravata iti prāṇān āha sapta vidyāt parāvata ity apānān āha / śiro yajñasya yo vidyād ity etad vai yajñasya śiro yan mantravān brahmaudano yo ha vā etam amantravantaṃ brahmaudanam upeyād apaśirasā ha vā asya yajñam upeto bhavati tasmān mantravantam eva brahmaudanam upeyān nāmantravantam iti brāhmaṇam // GpBr_1,2.16 //
children.translated_text: <s>Prajāpati Atharvan</s>, the divine one, having performed austerity (<s>tapas</s>), created this fourfold <s>Brahmaudana</s> (Brahman's rice porridge) — of four worlds, four gods, four <s>Vedas</s>, and four priestly offices. For these four worlds are: earth, atmosphere, heaven, and the waters. These four gods are: <s>Agni</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Āditya</s>, and <s>Candramās</s> (the Moon). These four <s>Vedas</s> are: the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, <s>Yajurveda</s>, <s>Sāmaveda</s>, and <s>Brahmaveda</s> [Atharvaveda]. These four priestly offices are: the <s>Hautra</s> (of the <s>Hotṛ</s>), the <s>Ādhvaryava</s> (of the <s>Adhvaryu</s>), the <s>Audgātra</s> (of the <s>Udgātṛ</s>), and the <s>Brahmatva</s> (of the <s>Brahman</s> priest). And this too is stated in the <s>ṛc</s>: 'Four horns, three feet has he, two heads, seven hands has he; bound threefold, the bull bellows; the great god has entered mortals.' 'Four horns' — these are the <s>Vedas</s> that are mentioned. 'Three feet' — these are the [three] <s>savana</s>s (pressings). 'Two heads' — these are the <s>Brahmaudana</s> and the <s>Pravargya</s>. 'Seven hands' — these are the meters (<s>chandas</s>). 'Bound threefold' — [these are] mantra, ritual application (<s>kalpa</s>), and <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. 'The bull bellows' — he indeed is the bull; he bellows because he recites the <s>śastra</s>s at sacrifices, with <s>ṛc</s>s, <s>yajus</s>es, <s>sāman</s>s, and <s>brahman</s>s. 'The great god has entered mortals' — the sacrifice is indeed the great god; he has entered mortals. 'He who would know the seven streams' — this refers to the <s>prāṇa</s>s. 'He who would know the seven distant [places]' — this refers to the <s>apāna</s>s. 'He who would know the head of the sacrifice' — this indeed is the head of the sacrifice: the <s>Brahmaudana</s> accompanied by mantras. He who would approach the <s>Brahmaudana</s> without mantras — his sacrifice is approached without a head. Therefore one should approach the <s>Brahmaudana</s> accompanied by mantras, not without mantras. Thus [says] the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. (GpBr 1,2.16)

children.text: kim upayajña ātreyo bhavatīty ādityaṃ hi tamo jagrāha tad atrir apanunoda tad atrir anvapaśyat / tad apy etad ṛcoktam / stutādyam atrir divam unnināya divitvātrir adhārayat sūryām āsāya kartava iti / taṃ hovāca varaṃ vṛṇīṣveti sa hovāca dakṣiṇīyā me prajā syād iti tasmād ātreyāya prathamadakṣiṇā yajñe dīyanta iti brāhmaṇam // GpBr_1,2.17 //
children.translated_text: Why does the son of <s>Atri</s> (<s>Ātreya</s>) become the subsidiary sacrificer? Because darkness seized the sun (<s>Āditya</s>); <s>Atri</s> drove it away; <s>Atri</s> perceived [the means to do so]. And this too is stated in the <s>ṛc</s>: '<s>Atri</s>, having praised him, lifted the sun to heaven; <s>Atri</s>, being celestial, upheld [the sun]; he placed the sun for the performer of rites.' [The sun] said to him: 'Choose a boon.' He said: 'May my offspring be worthy of the sacrificial fee (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>).' Therefore the first <s>dakṣiṇā</s> in a sacrifice is given to an <s>Ātreya</s>. Thus [says] the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. (GpBr 1,2.17)

children.text: prajāpatir vedān uvāca agnīn ādadhīyeti tān vāg abhyuvācāśvo vai sambhārāṇām iti taṃ ghorāt krūrāt salilāt sarasa udāninyus tān vāg abhyuvācāśvaḥ śamyeteti tatheti tam ṛgveda etyovācāham aśvaṃ śameyam iti tasmā avisṛptāya mahad bhayaṃ sasṛje sa etāṃ prācīṃ diśam bheje sa hovācāśānto nv ayam aśva iti / taṃ yajurveda etyovācāham aśvaṃ śameyam iti tasmā avisṛptāya mahad bhayaṃ sasṛje sā etāṃ pratīcīṃ diśaṃ bheje sa hovācāśānto nv ayam aśva iti / taṃ sāmaveda etyovācāham aśvaṃ śameyam iti kena nu tvaṃ śamayiṣyasīti rathaṃtaraṃ nāma me sāmāghoraṃ cākrūraṃ ca tenāśvam abhiṣṭūyate tasmā atha visṛptāya tad eva mahad bhayaṃ sasṛje sa etām udīcīṃ diśam bheje sa hovācāśānto nv ayam aśva iti / tān vāg abhyuvāca śaṃyum ātharvaṇaṃ gacchatheti te śaṃyum ātharvaṇam āsīnaṃ prāpyocur namas te astu bhagavann aśva śamyeteti / tatheti sa khalu kabandhasyātharvaṇasya putram āmantrayāmāsa vicārinn iti bhaga iti hāsmai pratiśrutaṃ pratiśuśrāvāśvaṃ śamyeteti tatheti sa khalu śāntyudakaṃ cakārātharvaṇobhiś cāṅgirasobhiś cātanair mātṛnāmabhir vāstoṣpatyair iti śamayati tasya ha snātasyāśvasyābhyukṣitasya sarvebhyo romaśamarebhyo 'ṅgārā āśīryanta so 'śvas tuṣṭo namaskāraṃ cakāra namaḥ śaṃyum ātharvaṇāya yo mā yajñam acīkṛpad iti bhaviṣyanti ha vā ato 'nye brāhmaṇā laghusambhāratamāsta ādityasya pada ādhāsyanty anaḍuho vatsasyājasya śravaṇasya brahmacāriṇo vā etad vā ādityasya padaṃ yad bhūmis tayaiva pada āhitaṃ bhaviṣyatīti so 'gnau praṇīyamāne 'śve 'nvārabdhaṃ brahmā yajamānaṃ vācayati yad akrandaḥ prathamaṃ jāyamāna iti pañca taṃ brāhmaṇā upavahanti tad brahmopākurute eṣa ha vai vidvāṃt sarvavid brahmā yad bhṛgvaṅgirovid iti brāhmaṇam // GpBr_1,2.18 //
children.translated_text: <s>Prajāpati</s> said to the <s>Veda</s>s: 'I wish to establish the [sacrificial] fires.' Speech addressed them: 'The horse indeed [is chief] among the ritual materials.' They led that [horse] out from the terrible, fierce, watery, marshy [place]. Speech addressed them: 'May the horse be pacified.' 'So be it.' The <s>Ṛgveda</s> came and said: 'I shall pacify the horse.' For him who had not yet released [the horse], a great fear was created. He fled to the eastern direction. He said: 'This horse is indeed not pacified.' The <s>Yajurveda</s> came and said: 'I shall pacify the horse.' For him who had not yet released [the horse], a great fear was created. It fled to the western direction. He said: 'This horse is indeed not pacified.' The <s>Sāmaveda</s> came and said: 'I shall pacify the horse.' 'By what means will you pacify it?' 'I have a <s>Sāman</s> (chant) called <s>Rathantara</s>, which is neither terrible nor fierce; by that [the horse] is praised.' For him who then released [the horse], that very great fear was created. He fled to the northern direction. He said: 'This horse is indeed not pacified.' Speech addressed them: 'Go to <s>Śaṃyu Ātharvaṇa</s> (the Pacifier of the <s>Atharvan</s> tradition).' Having reached <s>Śaṃyu Ātharvaṇa</s> seated [in his place], they said: 'Homage to you, O Blessed One! May the horse be pacified.' 'So be it.' He then summoned the son of <s>Kabandha Ātharvaṇa</s>: 'O <s>Vicārin</s> (Wanderer)!' 'Blessed One!' — was the reply he heard — 'May the horse be pacified.' 'So be it.' He indeed prepared the pacificatory water (<s>śāntyudaka</s>). With [the mantras of] the <s>Atharvan</s>s, the <s>Aṅgiras</s>es, the <s>Atana</s>s, the mother-named ones, and the <s>Vāstoṣpatya</s>s, he pacifies. When that horse was bathed and sprinkled, from all its hair-pores, coals fell forth. That horse, satisfied, made obeisance [saying]: 'Homage to <s>Śaṃyu Ātharvaṇa</s>, who made me fit for the sacrifice.' 'There will be henceforth other <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s who will establish [the fires] with the lightest of materials, in the footprint of the sun — [using] the bull, the calf, the goat, or the [month] <s>Śravaṇa</s>, or the <s>brahmacārin</s>. For this is the footprint of the sun — the earth; on that very footprint it will be established.' When the fire is being led forward and the horse has been grasped, the <s>Brahmán</s> (priest) makes the sacrificer recite: 'When you cried out being born for the first time.' Five <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s carry him. Then the <s>Brahmán</s> begins. He indeed is the learned, omniscient <s>Brahmán</s> priest who knows [the tradition of] <s>Bhṛgu</s> and <s>Aṅgiras</s> — thus [says] the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.

children.text:

children.translated_text: The <s>Deva</s>s (gods) and the <s>Asura</s>s (demons) were indeed contending. The <s>Deva</s>s said to <s>Indra</s>: 'Guard this sacrifice of ours while we fight against the <s>Asura</s>s.' 'Guard us in that form by which you cover us most and by which you will be able to protect [us].' He, having become the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, went around from the east and stood nearby. The <s>Deva</s>s said to him: 'Assume another form; by this form you do not cover us sufficiently, nor will you be able to protect [us] by it.' He, having become the <s>Yajurveda</s>, went around from the west and stood [there]. The <s>Deva</s>s said to him: 'Assume another form; by this form you do not cover us sufficiently, nor will you be able to protect [us] by it.' He, having become the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, went around from the north and stood [there]. The <s>Deva</s>s said to him: 'Assume yet another form; by this form you do not cover us sufficiently, nor will you be able to protect [us] by it.' He, <s>Indra</s>, wearing the turban (<s>uṣṇīṣin</s>), having become the <s>Brahmaveda</s> (the Veda of <s>Brahman</s>, i.e. the <s>Atharvaveda</s>), went around from the south and stood [there]. The <s>Deva</s>s said to him: 'Assume this very form; by this form you cover us most, by this you will be able to protect [us].' Because <s>Indra</s>, wearing the turban, having become the <s>Brahmaveda</s>, went around from the south and stood [there] — that became the <s>Brahman</s> [priest]; that is the <s>Brahman</s>-hood of the <s>Brahman</s> [priest]. This indeed is the form of the <s>Atharvan</s> — the <s>Brahman</s> [priest] who wears the turban. The <s>Viśvedeva</s>s (All-gods) sat beside him on the south; because the <s>Viśvedeva</s>s sat beside him on the south, that became the <s>Sadasya</s> (member of the sacrificial assembly); that is the <s>Sadasya</s>-hood of the <s>Sadasya</s>. From <s>Bali</s> (tribute) indeed this strength arises, which [belongs to] the <s>Sadasya</s>. From a diseased herd they select a more abundant herd. The southern direction is fierce; the others are peaceful. As for the hymns of praise (<s>stuta</s>s) that the <s>Brahman</s> [priest] approves, those the <s>Sadasya</s> [approves] by mind alone. By muttering the <s>vyāhṛti</s> (sacred utterance) '<s>janat</s>' (may he generate), he generates himself; he does not place his self in defeat. The <s>Deva</s>s said to him: 'Choose a boon.' 'I choose!' He chose the boon: 'In this very priestly office (<s>hotrā</s>), let them stand purifying, praising, and reciting me as having become <s>Indra</s>.' They stood in that very priestly office, purifying, praising, and reciting him as having become <s>Indra</s>. Because in that very priestly office they stood purifying, praising, and reciting him as having become <s>Indra</s>, that became the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s> (the one who recites for the <s>Brahman</s> priest); that is the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>-hood of the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin</s>. This is the priestly office belonging to <s>Indra</s>, namely the <s>Brāhmaṇācchaṃsī</s>. 'Choose a second boon.' 'I choose!' He chose the boon: 'In this very priestly office, let them stand purifying, praising, and reciting me as having become <s>Vāyu</s> (wind).' They stood in that very priestly office, purifying, praising, and reciting him as having become <s>Vāyu</s>. Because in that very priestly office they stood purifying, praising, and reciting him as having become <s>Vāyu</s>, that became the <s>Potṛ</s> (the purifier priest); that is the <s>Potṛ</s>-hood of the <s>Potṛ</s>. This is the priestly office belonging to <s>Vāyu</s>, namely the <s>Potrī</s>. 'Choose a third boon.' 'I choose!' He chose the boon: 'In this very priestly office, let them stand kindling, purifying, praising, and reciting me as having become <s>Agni</s> (fire).' They stood in that very priestly office, kindling, purifying, praising, and reciting him as having become <s>Agni</s>. Because in that very priestly office they stood kindling, purifying, praising, and reciting him as having become <s>Agni</s>, that became the <s>Āgnīdhra</s> (the fire-kindler priest); that is the <s>Āgnīdhra</s>-hood of the <s>Āgnīdhra</s>. This is the priestly office belonging to <s>Agni</s>, namely the <s>Āgnīdhrī</s> — thus [says] the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [text].

children.text: brāhmaṇo ha vā imam agniṃ vaiśvānaraṃ babhāra / so 'yam agnir vaiśvānaro brāhmaṇena bhriyamāṇa imāṃl lokān janayate 'thāyam īkṣate 'gnir jātavedā brāhmaṇadvitīyo ha vā ayam idam agnir vaiśvānaro jvalati hantāhaṃ yan mayi teja indriyaṃ vīryaṃ tad darśayāmy uta vai mā bibhriyād iti sa ātmānam āpyāyayet taṃ payo 'dhok tam imaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ darśayitvātmany ajuhot sa dvitīyam ātmānam āpyāyayet taṃ ghṛtam adhok tam imaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ darśayitvātmany ajuhot sa tṛtīyam ātmānam āpyāyayet tad idaṃ viśvaṃ vikṛtam annādyam adhok tam imaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ darśayitvātmany ajuhot sa caturtham ātmānam āpyāyayet tena brāhmaṇasya jāyāṃ virājam apaśyat tām asmai prāyacchat sa ātmā apitvam abhavat tata imam agniṃ vaiśvānaraṃ parāsyur brāhmaṇo 'gniṃ jātavedasam adhatta so 'yam abravīt agne jātavedo 'bhinidhehi mehīti tasya dvaitaṃ nāmādhattāghoraṃ cākrūraṃ ca so 'śvo 'bhavat tasmād aśvo vaheta rathaṃ na bhavati pṛṣṭhena sādinaṃ sa devān āgacchat sa devebhyo 'nvātiṣṭhat tasmād devā abibhayus taṃ brahmaṇe prāyacchat tam etayarcāśamayat // GpBr_1,2.20 //
children.translated_text: A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> indeed bore this fire, <s>Vaiśvānara</s>. This fire, <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, being borne by the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, generates these worlds. Then this one [Agni] reflected: 'Fire <s>Jātavedas</s>, with the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> as my companion — this fire <s>Vaiśvānara</s> blazes. Come, let me display whatever splendor, vitality, and power is in me; perhaps he would bear me.' He nourished himself: he milked forth milk. Having shown it to this <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, he offered it into himself. He nourished himself a second time: he milked forth ghee. Having shown it to this <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, he offered it into himself. He nourished himself a third time: from this he milked forth all this manifold food. Having shown it to this <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, he offered it into himself. He nourished himself a fourth time: thereby he beheld <s>Virāj</s>, the wife of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. He gave her to him. He, the Self, became intimate [with her]. Then they cast aside this fire <s>Vaiśvānara</s>. The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> took up <s>Agni Jātavedas</s>. He [Agni] said: 'O <s>Agni Jātavedas</s>, kindle me here!' He gave it two names: <s>Aghora</s> (not terrible) and <s>Akrūra</s> (not cruel). It became a horse. Therefore the horse carries a chariot but does not become [merely] a mount for a rider on its back. It approached the gods; it stood among the gods. Therefore the gods were afraid. They gave it to <s>Brahman</s> [the priest]. With this <s>ṛc</s> [verse] he pacified it. (GpBr 1,2.20)

naiva gāyen nānṛtyen māglāgṛdhaḥ syāt tasmād brāhmyaṃ pūrvaṃ havir aparaṃ prājāpatyaṃ prājāpatyāt brāhmaṇam evottamam iti brāhmaṇam // GpBr_1,2.21 //
children.translated_text: should neither sing nor dance, lest he become consumed by the flame of impurity (<s>āglāgṛdha</s>). Therefore the offering to <s>Brahman</s> is first, and the subsequent one is to <s>Prajāpati</s>; [but] the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is indeed supreme over [even] the <s>Prājāpatya</s> [offering]. Thus [says] the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. (GpBr 1,2.21)

'They call <s>Agni</s> <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, burning forth from its seat, leaving behind; tell us of the divine, O esteemed one, we are yours' — with these five <s>ṛc</s>s he begins [the rite]: 'When you cried out, being born for the first time.' It [the horse/fire] became calm. Therefore the horse, among animals, is the most desirous of eating, for it is <s>Vaiśvānara</s>. Therefore <s>Agni</s>, having its place, gives the horse to the <s>Brahman</s> [priest], for it was given to <s>Brahman</s>. He pressed out its essence (<s>rasa</s>); that essence came into being — the essence indeed is this. They call that existing essence 'chariot' (<s>ratha</s>) — by indirection, for the gods are fond of the indirect and averse to the direct. It approached the gods; it stood among the gods; therefore the gods were afraid. They gave it to <s>Brahman</s> [the priest]. With this <s>ṛc</s> and with a ghee-oblation he offered: '<s>Indra</s>'s might, the vanguard of the <s>Marut</s>s.' Having offered to the chariot, with this <s>ṛc</s> he stood firm: 'O tree, may you be strong-limbed!' Therefore one gives the chariot from the fire-placing to the <s>Brahman</s> priest, for it was given to <s>Brahman</s>. The craftsmen fashioned the eldest-born <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (priestly fee). He perceived it in five [forms]: in the <s>ṛc</s>, <s>yajus</s>, <s>sāman</s>, in the peaceful, and in the terrible. Of those, he gave two to the <s>Brahman</s> priest: Speech and Light. Speech is the cow; Light is gold. Therefore one gives the cow of the fourfold <s>Brahmaudana</s> at the fire-placing to the <s>Brahman</s> priest, for it was given to <s>Brahman</s>. When the animals are being pacified, they remove sight [from them]; he then places sight in himself. What is sight — that is gold. Therefore one gives gold at the fire-placing to the <s>Brahman</s> priest, for it was given to <s>Brahman</s>. He placed [part of the dakṣiṇā] in himself; with that he blazed forth. What he did not place — that became the <s>āglā</s> (flame of impurity). That <s>āglā</s>, having come into being, entered the ocean; it burned the ocean — therefore the ocean is difficult to cross, for it was burned by <s>Vaiśvānara</s>. It came up to the earth; it burned through the earth. It reached the gods; it scorched the gods. The gods ran to <s>Brahman</s>. He [the Brahman priest] neither sang nor danced. This is the <s>āglā</s>; this is called <s>Kāruvid</s>. They call that [Brahman priest] who is scorched by the <s>āglā</s> '<s>āglāgṛdha</s>' (consumed by the flame of impurity) — by indirection, for the gods are fond of the indirect and averse to the direct. A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who sings or dances is called <s>āglāgṛdha</s>. Therefore a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>

children.text: atharvāṇaś ca ha vā āṅgirasaś ca bhṛgucakṣuṣī tad brahmābhivyapaśyaṃs tad ajānan vayaṃ vā idaṃ sarvaṃ yad bhṛgvaṅgirasa iti / te devā brāhmyaṃ havir yat sāṃtapane 'gnāv ajuhavur etad vai brāhmyaṃ havir yat sāṃtapane 'gnau hūyate eṣa ha vai sāṃtapano 'gnir yad brāhmaṇas tasyorjayorjāṃ devā abhajanta sumanasa eva svadhāṃ pitaraḥ śraddhayā svargaṃ lokaṃ brāhmaṇās tena sunvanty ṛṣayo 'ntataḥ striyaḥ kevala ātmany avārundhata vāhyā ubhayena sunvanti yad vai yajñe brāhmyaṃ havir na nirūpyetānṛjavaḥ prājāpatyahaviṣo manuṣyā jāyerann asau yāṃl lokān śṛṇv iti pitā hy eṣa āhavanīyasya gārhapatyasya dakṣiṇāgner yo 'gnihotraṃ juhotīti vā priye dhāmani madanti teṣām eṣo 'gniḥ sāṃtapanaśreṣṭho bhavaty etasya vāci tṛptāyām agnis tṛpyati prāṇe tṛpte vāyus tṛpyati cakṣuṣī tṛpta ādityas tṛpyati manasi tṛpte candramās tṛpyati śrotre tṛpte diśaś cāntardeśāś ca tṛpyanti sneheṣu tṛpteṣv āpas tṛpyanti lomeṣu tṛpteṣv oṣadhivanaspatayas tṛpyanti śarīre tṛpte pṛthivī tṛpyaty evam eṣo 'gniḥ sāṃtapanaḥ śreṣṭhas tṛptaḥ sarvās tṛptās tarpayatīti brāhmaṇam // GpBr_1,2.22 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Atharvans</s> and the <s>Āṅgirasas</s> are indeed the eyes of <s>Bhṛgu</s>. <s>Brahman</s>, looking forth through them, recognized: 'We are indeed all this — we who are the <s>Bhṛgvaṅgirasas</s>.' The gods offered the Brāhmaṇic oblation in the <s>Sāṃtapana</s> (heating) fire. This is indeed the Brāhmaṇic oblation which is offered in the <s>Sāṃtapana</s> fire. This <s>Sāṃtapana</s> fire is indeed the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. Of his nourishment, the gods partook of his vigor; the well-minded ancestors [partook of] the funerary offering (<s>svadhā</s>); with faith the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> [attain] the heavenly world; by that the <s>ṛṣis</s> (seers) press [the Soma]; women [partake] of themselves alone; those who are excluded [partake] by both means — they press. If indeed the Brāhmaṇic oblation is not offered at the sacrifice, crooked people would be born, [eating only] the oblation of <s>Prajāpati</s>. 'Hear, O father, what worlds [there are]' — for he is the father of the <s>Āhavanīya</s>, the <s>Gārhapatya</s>, and the <s>Dakṣiṇāgni</s> — 'whoever offers the <s>Agnihotra</s>' — indeed they rejoice in the beloved abode. Of these, this <s>Sāṃtapana</s> fire is the most excellent. When his speech is satisfied, <s>Agni</s> is satisfied; when breath is satisfied, <s>Vāyu</s> is satisfied; when sight is satisfied, <s>Āditya</s> is satisfied; when mind is satisfied, <s>Candramās</s> (the moon) is satisfied; when hearing is satisfied, the directions and the intermediate directions are satisfied; when the body-fluids are satisfied, the waters are satisfied; when the body-hairs are satisfied, herbs and trees are satisfied; when the body is satisfied, the earth is satisfied. Thus this most excellent <s>Sāṃtapana</s> fire, when satisfied, satisfies all — thus [says] the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. // GpBr 1,2.22 //

children.text: sāṃtapanā idaṃ havir ity eṣa ha vai sāṃtapano 'gnir yad brāhmaṇo yasya garbhādhānapuṃsavanasīmantonnayanajātakarmanāmakaraṇaniṣkramaṇānnaprāśanagodānacūḍākaraṇopanayanāplavanāgnihotravratacaryādīnikṛtāni bhavanti sa sāṃtapano 'tha yo 'yam anagnikaḥ sa kumbhe tad yathā kumbhe loṣṭaḥ prakṣipto naiva śaucārthāya kalpate naiva śasyaṃ nirvartayaty evam evāyaṃ brāhmo 'nagnikas tasya brāhmaṇasyānagnikasya naiva daivaṃ dadyān na pitryaṃ na cāsya svādhyāyāśiṣo na yajña āśiṣaḥ svargaṃgamā bhavanti / tad apy etad ṛcoktam / agniṃ dūtaṃ vṛṇīmahe hotāraṃ viśvavedasam / asya yajñasya sukratum iti brāhmaṇam // GpBr_1,2.23 //
children.translated_text: 'To the <s>Sāṃtapana</s>, this oblation' — this <s>Sāṃtapana</s> fire is indeed the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> for whom the rites of <s>garbhādhāna</s> (conception), <s>puṃsavana</s> (rite for male offspring), <s>sīmantonnyana</s> (hair-parting ceremony), <s>jātakarma</s> (birth rite), <s>nāmakaraṇa</s> (naming ceremony), <s>niṣkramaṇa</s> (first outing), <s>annaprāśana</s> (first feeding), <s>godāna</s> (cow-gift ceremony), <s>cūḍākaraṇa</s> (tonsure), <s>upanayana</s> (initiation), <s>āplavana</s> (concluding bath), <s>agnihotra</s> (fire oblation), <s>vratacarya</s> (observance of vows), and so forth have been performed — he is the <s>Sāṃtapana</s>. Now <s>Prajāpati</s>, about to sacrifice with <s>Soma</s>, said to the <s>Veda</s>s: 'Whom shall I choose as your <s>hotṛ</s> (invoking priest)? Whom as <s>adhvaryu</s> (officiating priest)? Whom as <s>udgātṛ</s> (chanting priest)? Whom as <s>brahmán</s> (supervising priest)?' They said: 'Choose a knower of the <s>Ṛgveda</s> as <s>hotṛ</s>, a knower of the <s>Yajurveda</s> as <s>adhvaryu</s>, a knower of the <s>Sāmaveda</s> as <s>udgātṛ</s>, and a knower of the <s>Atharvāṅgiras</s> as <s>brahmán</s>. Thus his sacrifice, [established] in four worlds, in four gods, in four <s>Veda</s>s, in four priestly offices, becomes four-footed. The sacrifice is firmly established; one is firmly established with offspring and cattle — whoever knows this.' 'Therefore choose a knower of the <s>Ṛgveda</s> as <s>hotṛ</s>, for he knows the <s>hautra</s> (invocative) office. <s>Agni</s> indeed is the <s>hotṛ</s>; the earth is the abode of the <s>Ṛc</s> verses; <s>Agni</s> is the deity; <s>Gāyatrī</s> is the meter; '<s>Bhūḥ</s>' is the bright [utterance]. Therefore choose him as <s>hotṛ</s>' — for the conquest of this world, for the complete conquest, for the thorough conquest, for the possession, for the increase, for the flourishing, for the elevation, for the pervasion, for the sufficiency, for the completion of this world. But if one does not choose such a knower as <s>hotṛ</s>, their sacrifice is deficient from the east. Therefore choose him as <s>adhvaryu</s>' — for [the conquest etc.] of this world — and so on. But if one does not choose such a knower as <s>adhvaryu</s>, their sacrifice is deficient from the west.
