children.translated_text: Oṃ. The earth slopes southward, the waters flow to the south; therefore the sacrificial ground is as though elevated above that earth where the <s>Bhṛgvaṅgiras</s> are stationed. Just as the waters carry these worlds, so indeed the <s>Bhṛgvaṅgiras</s> carry all the gods; just so this <s>Vyāhṛti</s> (sacred utterance) carries all the <s>Vedas</s>. 'Oṃ' belongs to the <s>Ṛc</s> verses, 'Oṃ' to the <s>Yajus</s> formulae, 'Oṃ' to the <s>Sāman</s> chants — 'Oṃ' is the salutation of all. The learned ones make this supreme in the sacrifice: 'O divine <s>Brahmans</s>, come, come!' These divine <s>Brahmans</s> are indeed the <s>Bhṛgvaṅgiras</s>; praising them, choosing them, calling them — they think thus. No one other than a knower of <s>Bhṛgvaṅgiras</s>, having been chosen, should come to the sacrifice; by the splendor of the sacrifice he attains splendor, by its vigor he attains vigor, by its glory he attains glory. No one other than a knower of <s>Bhṛgvaṅgiras</s>, uninvited, should come to the sacrifice, lest he steal from the sacrifice. Just as a calf, having first suckled, would milk the cow — so a <s>Brahman</s> who is a knower of <s>Bhṛgvaṅgiras</s>, uninvited, should come to the sacrifice, lest he steal from the sacrifice. Just as a cow, or a horse, or a mule — whether one-footed, two-footed, or three-footed — what could it carry? What could it attain? Therefore, choose as <s>Hotṛ</s> one who knows the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, as <s>Adhvaryu</s> one who knows the <s>Yajurveda</s>, as <s>Udgātṛ</s> one who knows the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, and as <s>Brahman</s> one who knows the <s>Atharvāṅgiras</s>. Thus his sacrifice, established in the four worlds, in the four gods, in the four <s>Vedas</s>, in the four priestly offices — the four-footed sacrifice becomes firmly established. He becomes established with offspring and cattle who knows thus, and who knows the priestly function of the <s>ṛtvij</s> priests, and who knows what is worthy of worship in the sacrifice — thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. // <s>GpBr</s> 1.3.1 //

children.text: prajāpatir yajñam atanuta sa ṛcaiva hautram akarot yajuṣādhvaryavaṃ sāmnaudgātram atharvāṅgirobhir brahmatvaṃ taṃ vā etaṃ mahāvādyaṃ kurute yad ṛcaiva hautram akarod yajuṣādhvaryavaṃ sāmnaudgātram atharvāṅgirobhir brahmatvaṃ sa vā eṣa tribhir vedair yajñasyānyataraḥ pakṣaḥ saṃskriyate manasaiva brahmā yajñasyānyataraṃ pakṣaṃ saṃskaroty ayam u vai yaḥ pavate sa yajñas tasya manaś ca vāk ca vartanir manasā caiva hi vācā ca yajñe vahaty ata eva mana iyam eva vāk sa yad vadan nāsti vidyād ardhaṃ me 'sya yajñasyāntaragād iti tad yathaikapāt puruṣo yann ekacakro vā ratho vartamāno bhreṣaṃ nyety evam evāsya yajño bhreṣaṃ nyeti yajñasya bhreṣam anu yajamāno bhreṣaṃ nyeti yajamānasya bhreṣam anv ṛtvijo bhreṣaṃ niyanti ṛtvijāṃ bhreṣam anu dakṣiṇā bhreṣaṃ niyanti dakṣiṇānāṃ bhreṣam anu yajamānaḥ putrapaśubhir bhreṣaṃ nyeti putrapaśūnāṃ bhreṣam anu yajamānaḥ svargeṇa lokena bhreṣaṃ nyeti svargasya lokasya bhreṣam anu tasyārdhasya yogakṣemo bhreṣaṃ nyeti yasminn ardhe yajanta iti brāhmaṇam // GpBr_1,3.2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Prajāpati</s> extended the sacrifice. With the <s>Ṛc</s> alone he performed the <s>Hautra</s> (office of the <s>Hotṛ</s>), with the <s>Yajus</s> the <s>Ādhvaryava</s> (office of the <s>Adhvaryu</s>), with the <s>Sāman</s> the <s>Audgātra</s> (office of the <s>Udgātṛ</s>), and with the <s>Atharvāṅgiras</s> the <s>Brahmatva</s> (office of the <s>Brahman</s> priest). He indeed performs this great declaration: that with the <s>Ṛc</s> alone he performed the <s>Hautra</s>, with the <s>Yajus</s> the <s>Ādhvaryava</s>, with the <s>Sāman</s> the <s>Audgātra</s>, and with the <s>Atharvāṅgiras</s> the <s>Brahmatva</s>. One wing of his sacrifice is fashioned by the three <s>Vedas</s>; the <s>Brahman</s> priest fashions the other wing of the sacrifice with mind alone. Now, that which blows (the wind) is the sacrifice; mind and speech are its two tracks, for with mind and speech indeed one carries forth in the sacrifice. Mind is this one, speech is that one. If the speaking one is absent, one should know: 'Half of my sacrifice has gone inside.' Just as a one-footed person walking, or a one-wheeled chariot rolling, goes to ruin — so his sacrifice goes to ruin. Following the sacrifice's ruin, the sacrificer goes to ruin; following the sacrificer's ruin, the <s>ṛtvij</s> priests go to ruin; following the priests' ruin, the sacrificial fees go to ruin; following the fees' ruin, the sacrificer with his sons and cattle goes to ruin; following that, the sacrificer's heavenly world goes to ruin; following the heavenly world's ruin, the welfare of that half goes to ruin — that half in which they sacrifice — thus is the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. // <s>GpBr</s> 1.3.2 //

children.text: tad u ha smāha śvetaketur āruṇeyo brahmāṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhāṣamāṇam ardhaṃ me 'sya yajñasyāntaragād iti tasmād brahmā stute bahiḥ pavamāne vācoyamyam upāṃśvantaryāmābhyām atha ye pavamāna udūcus teṣv atha yāni ca stotrāṇi ca śastrāṇy ā vaṣaṭkārāt teṣu sa yad ṛkto bhreṣaṃ niyacched oṃ bhūr janad iti gārhapatye juhuyāt yadi yajuṣṭa oṃ bhuvo janad iti dakṣiṇāgnau juhuyāt yadi sāmata oṃ svar janad ity āhavanīye juhuyāt yady anājñātā brahmatā oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svar janad oṃ ity āhavanīya eva juhuyāt tadvākovākyasyarcāṃ yajuṣāṃ sāmnām atharvāṅgirasām athopa vedānāṃ rasena yajñasya viriṣṭaṃ saṃdhīyate tad yathā lavaṇenety uktaṃ tad yathā ubhayapāt puruṣo yann ubhayacakro vā ratho vartamāno 'bhreṣaṃ nyety evam evāsya yajño 'bhreṣaṃ nyeti yajñasyābhreṣam anu yajamāno 'bhreṣaṃ nyeti yajamānasyābhreṣam anv ṛtvijo 'bhreṣaṃ niyanti ṛtvijām abhreṣam anu dakṣiṇā abhreṣaṃ niyanti dakṣiṇānām abhreṣam anu yajamānaḥ putrapaśubhir abhreṣaṃ nyeti putrapaśūnām abhreṣam anu yajamānaḥ svargeṇa lokenābhreṣaṃ nyeti svargasya lokasyābhreṣam anu tasyārdhasya yogakṣemo 'bhreṣaṃ nyeti yasminn ardhe yajanta iti brāhmaṇam // GpBr_1,3.3 //
children.translated_text: Now, <s>Śvetaketu Āruṇeya</s> said, upon seeing the <s>Brahman</s> [priest] speaking: 'Half of this sacrifice of mine has gone astray!' Therefore the <s>Brahman</s> [priest] should restrain his speech during the <s>stuta</s> (hymn of praise) at the outer <s>Pavamāna</s> (purification chant), [and] during the <s>Upāṃśu</s> and <s>Antaryāma</s> [pressings]. Then [he should be silent] during those [chants] that were sung aloud in the <s>Pavamāna</s>, and during those <s>stotra</s>s (hymns of praise) and <s>śastra</s>s (recitations) up to the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> (sacrificial exclamation). If there is a fault from the <s>Ṛc</s> (verse), he should offer [saying] '<s>Oṃ bhūr janat</s>' in the <s>Gārhapatya</s> [fire]. If from the <s>Yajus</s> (sacrificial formula), he should offer [saying] '<s>Oṃ bhuvo janat</s>' in the <s>Dakṣiṇāgni</s> (southern fire). If from the <s>Sāman</s> (chant), he should offer [saying] '<s>Oṃ svar janat</s>' in the <s>Āhavanīya</s> [fire]. If the nature of the fault of the <s>Brahman</s> [priest] is unknown, he should offer [saying] '<s>Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svar janad oṃ</s>' in the <s>Āhavanīya</s> alone. That is the dialogue of the <s>Ṛc</s>s, <s>Yajus</s>es, <s>Sāman</s>s, and <s>Atharvāṅgiras</s>es; and by the essence of the <s>Upa-Veda</s>s, the injury to the sacrifice is healed. As was said, 'just as with salt' — just as a two-footed man walking, or a two-wheeled chariot moving, proceeds without fault, even so his sacrifice proceeds without fault. Following the faultlessness of the sacrifice, the sacrificer proceeds without fault. Following the faultlessness of the sacrificer, the <s>ṛtvij</s>s (priests) proceed without fault. Following the faultlessness of the priests, the <s>dakṣiṇā</s>s (sacrificial fees) proceed without fault. Following the faultlessness of the fees, the sacrificer proceeds without fault with sons and cattle. Following the faultlessness of sons and cattle, the sacrificer proceeds without fault to the heavenly world. Following the faultlessness of the heavenly world, the prosperity and security of that portion proceed without fault — the portion in which they sacrifice — thus [says] the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [text].

children.translated_text: Now, [concerning the Brahman priest's fees:] 'He sat on the <s>audumbarī</s> (fig-wood seat) for me, he sang the <s>hiṅkāra</s> for me, he gave the introduction (<s>prastāva</s>) for me, he sat amid the waters for me, he called the <s>Subrahmaṇyā</s> [invocation] for me' — [for these] the <s>dakṣiṇā</s>s (fees) are given to the <s>Udgātṛ</s> (chanter). 'He drew the cups (<s>graha</s>s) for me, he served for me, he made [the gods] listen for me, he concentrated the mind for me, he sacrificed for me, he recited for me, he uttered the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> for me' — [these fees go] to the <s>Adhvaryu</s> (officiant). 'He sat on the <s>Hotṛ</s>'s seat, he sacrificed for me, he recited for me, he uttered the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> for me' — [these fees go] to the <s>Hotṛ</s> (invoker). 'He arranged the sacrificial ground (<s>devayajana</s>) for me, the <s>Brahman</s> [priest] made the assembly-hall (<s>sadas</s>) for me, he muttered the <s>Brahma</s>-prayers for me, he offered the preliminary oblations and the concluding oblations for me, he sacrificed for me, he recited for me, he uttered the <s>vaṣaṭkāra</s> for me' — [these go] to the <s>Brahman</s> [priest]. 'He accomplished the greatest for me through <s>Brahman</s> (sacred knowledge).' For this indeed is the greatest <s>Brahman</s>: the <s>Bhṛgvaṅgiras</s>es. Those who are <s>Aṅgiras</s>es — they are the essence (<s>rasa</s>). Those who are <s>Atharvan</s>s — that is the medicine (<s>bheṣaja</s>). That which is medicine is immortality (<s>amṛta</s>). That which is immortality is <s>Brahman</s>. He [the Brahman priest] indeed [receives] half the share of the former priests, and half [the share] of the remaining ones — [that is] the <s>Brahman</s> [priest's portion] — thus [says] the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [text].

children.text: devāś ca ha vā asurāś ca saṃgrāmaṃ samayatanta tatraitās tistro hotrakā jihmaṃ pratipedire tāsām indra ucchāni sāmāni lulopa tāni hotre prāyacchad ājyaṃ ha vai hotur babhūva praugaṃ potur vaiśvadevaṃ ha vai hotur babhūva niṣkevalyaṃ neṣṭur marutvatīyaṃ ha vai hotur babhūva āgnimārutam āgnīdhrasya tasmād etad abhyastataram iva śasyate yad āgnimārutaṃ yasmād ete saṃśaṃsukā iva bhavanti yaddhotā potā neṣṭāgnīdhro mumohe vasīta tad brahmeyasām ivāsa tāsām ardhaṃ pratilulopa prathamārhaṇaṃ ca prathamapadaṃ caitad dakṣiṇāṃ caitat pariśiṣeded iti brāhmaṇam // GpBr_1,3.5 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Deva</s>s (gods) and the <s>Asura</s>s (demons) indeed joined in battle. In that [conflict], these three priestly offices (<s>hotraka</s>s) went astray. <s>Indra</s> cut away the exalted <s>Sāman</s> hymns from them and gave them to the <s>Hotṛ</s> (invoker). The <s>Ājya</s> [recitation] had indeed belonged to the <s>Hotṛ</s>; the <s>Prauga</s> [belonged] to the <s>Potṛ</s>; the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> [recitation] had indeed belonged to the <s>Hotṛ</s>; the <s>Niṣkevalya</s> [belonged] to the <s>Neṣṭṛ</s>; the <s>Mārutvatīya</s> [recitation] had indeed belonged to the <s>Hotṛ</s>; the <s>Āgnimāruta</s> [belonged] to the <s>Āgnīdhra</s>. Therefore the <s>Āgnimāruta</s> is recited in a somewhat overlapping manner, because they become, as it were, co-reciters — the <s>Hotṛ</s>, <s>Potṛ</s>, <s>Neṣṭṛ</s>, and <s>Āgnīdhra</s>. [<s>Indra</s>] would have worn confusion [as a garment]; that would have been like <s>Brahman</s> for those [offices]. He took back half of them — the right of first offering and the first portion — and this is the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (fee), and this [is what] remains — thus [says] the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [text].

children.text: uddālako ha vā āruṇir udīcyān vṛto dhāvayāṃcakāra tasya ha niṣka upāhito babhūva upavādād bibhyato yo mā brāhmaṇo 'nūcāna upavadiṣyati tasmā etaṃ pradāsyāmīti taddhodīcyān brāhmaṇān bhayaṃ bibheda uddālako ha vā ayam āyāti kaurupāñcālī brahmā brahmaputraḥ sa ūrdhvaṃ vṛto na paryādadhīta kenemaṃ vīreṇa prati saṃyatāmahā iti taṃ yata eva prapannaṃ dadhre tata evam anupratipedire taṃ ha svaidāyanaṃ śaunakam ūcuḥ svaidāyana tvaṃ vai no brahmiṣṭho 'sīti tvayemaṃ vīreṇa pratisayatāmahā iti taṃ yata eva prapannaṃ dadhre tata evam anupratipedire taṃ ha svaidāyanā ity āmantrayāmāsa sa ho gotamasya putretīti hāsmā asūyāt pratiśrutaṃ pratiśuśrāva sa vai gautamasya putra ūrdhvaṃ vṛto 'dhāvīt // GpBr_1,3.6 //
children.translated_text: <s>Uddālaka Āruṇi</s> indeed, having been elected [as the best debater] among the northerners, conducted a [learned] tournament. A gold necklace (<s>niṣka</s>) had been set up as [the prize] by him, fearing reproach: 'Whoever among learned <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> defeats me in debate, to him I shall give this [necklace].' That indeed struck fear among the northern <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>: 'This <s>Uddālaka</s> is coming — a <s>Kuru-Pañcāla</s> <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the son of <s>Brahman</s>. He has been elected [as supreme]; he would not be surpassed. By what hero shall we oppose him?' Wherever he arrived, they received him and thus submitted. They said to <s>Svaidāyana Śaunaka</s>: 'O <s>Svaidāyana</s>, you are indeed the most learned in <s>Brahman</s> among us; by you, with heroism, let him be opposed.' Wherever he arrived, they received him and thus submitted. He [Uddālaka] addressed him: 'O <s>Svaidāyana</s>!' But he [Svaidāyana] became offended [saying]: '[He calls me merely] the son of <s>Gotama</s>!' He heard the reply. That son of <s>Gautama</s>, having been elected [supreme], ran [the tournament] to the end. (GpBr 1,3.6)
